refs.text_gb: 你要对以色列人说，人许特别的愿，所许的人要按你所估的价值归给耶和华。
refs.text_big5: 你要對以色列人說，人許特別的願，所許的人要按你所估的價值歸給耶和華。
refs.text_en: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them, When a man makes a special vow, the persons shall be for Jehovah according to your valuation of persons

refs.text_gb: 你要对以色列人说，无论男女许了特别的愿，就是拿细耳人的愿，要将自己分别出来归给耶和华，
refs.text_big5: 你要對以色列人說，無論男女許了特別的願，就是拿細耳人的願，要將自己分別出來歸給耶和華，
refs.text_en: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them, When a man or a woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazarite, to separate himself to Jehovah,

refs.text_gb: 若从牛群羊群中取牛羊作火祭，献给耶和华，无论是燔祭或是别的祭，为要许特别的愿，或是作甘心祭，或是在所定节期献的，都要奉给耶和华为怡爽的香气；
refs.text_big5: 若從牛群羊群中取牛羊作火祭，獻給耶和華，無論是燔祭或是別的祭，為要許特別的願，或是作甘心祭，或是在所定節期獻的，都要奉給耶和華為怡爽的香氣；
refs.text_en: And you make an offering by fire to Jehovah, a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to make a special vow or as a freewill offering or at your appointed feasts, to make a satisfying fragrance to Jehovah, from the herd or from the flock,

refs.text_gb: 你预备公牛犊作燔祭，或是作别的祭，为要许特别的愿，或是作平安祭，献给耶和华，
refs.text_big5: 你豫備公牛犢作燔祭，或是作別的祭，為要許特別的願，或是作平安祭，獻給耶和華，
refs.text_en: And when you prepare a herd animal for a burnt offering or for a sacrifice, to make a special vow or for peace offerings to Jehovah,

refs.text_gb: 你要对亚伦和他儿子们，并以色列众人说，以色列家中的人，或在以色列中寄居的，凡献供物，无论是为许愿，或是甘心献的，就是献给耶和华作燔祭的，
refs.text_big5: 你要對亞倫和他兒子們，並以色列眾人說，以色列家中的人，或在以色列中寄居的，凡獻供物，無論是為許願，或是甘心獻的，就是獻給耶和華作燔祭的，
refs.text_en: Speak to Aaron and to his sons and to all the children of Israel, and say to them, When anyone of the house of Israel or of the sojourners in Israel presents his offering, whether it is any of their vows or any of their freewill offerings which they present to Jehovah for a burnt offering;

verses.text_gb: 瞎眼的、折伤的、残废的、有瘤子的、长癣的、长疥的，都不可献给耶和华，也不可在坛上作为火祭献给耶和华。
verses.text_big5: 瞎眼的、折傷的、殘廢的、有瘤子的、長癬的、長疥的，都不可獻給耶和華，也不可在壇上作為火祭獻給耶和華。
verses.text_en: You shall not present these to Jehovah: anything blind or injured or maimed or having a suppuration or eczema or scale; nor shall you make an offering by fire from them on the altar to Jehovah.
verses.text_gb_plain: 瞎眼的、折伤的、残废的、有瘤子的、长癣的、长疥的，都不可献给耶和华，也不可在坛上作为火祭献给耶和华。
verses.text_big5_plain: 瞎眼的、折傷的、殘廢的、有瘤子的、長癬的、長疥的，都不可獻給耶和華，也不可在壇上作為火祭獻給耶和華。

verses.text_gb: 无论是牛或羊，若肢体[Fn1]有余或缺少的，只可作甘心祭献上；若用以许愿，就不蒙悦纳。
verses.text_big5: 無論是牛或羊，若肢體[Fn1]有餘或缺少的，只可作甘心祭獻上；若用以許願，就不蒙悅納。
verses.text_en: An ox or a lamb that has anything superfluous or lacking in its parts, that you may offer for a freewill offering; but it shall not be accepted for a vow.
verses.text_gb_plain: 无论是牛或羊，若肢体有余或缺少的，只可作甘心祭献上；若用以许愿，就不蒙悦纳。
verses.text_big5_plain: 無論是牛或羊，若肢體有餘或缺少的，只可作甘心祭獻上；若用以許願，就不蒙悅納。

footnotes.zh: 有余，意思是超过限度；缺少，意思是不够适当的量。本节的话表征，我们可以普通的(作甘心祭)将自己所经历太多或太少的基督献给神作食物；但若要更强的献上(用以许愿)，我们的供物就不蒙悦纳。
footnotes.zh_big5: 有餘，意思是超過限度；缺少，意思是不彀適當的量。本節的話表徵，我們可以普通的（作甘心祭）將自己所經歷太多或太少的基督獻給神作食物；但若要更強的獻上（用以許願，）我們的供物就不蒙悅納。
footnotes.en: 22:23 1 superfluous Superfluous means exceeding the limit, and lacking means being under the proper measure. The word in this verse signifies that we may, in a general way (as a freewill offering), offer to God as food the Christ whom we experience too much or too little, but if we offer in a stronger way (as a vow), our offering will not be accepted.

verses.text_gb: 凡外肾损伤、或压碎、或破裂、或割除的，不可献给耶和华；在你们的地上不可这样行。
verses.text_big5: 凡外腎損傷、或壓碎、或破裂、或割除的，不可獻給耶和華；在你們的地上不可這樣行。
verses.text_en: And anything with its testicles bruised or crushed or broken or cut, you shall not present to Jehovah; you shall not do this in your land.
verses.text_gb_plain: 凡外肾损伤、或压碎、或破裂、或割除的，不可献给耶和华；在你们的地上不可这样行。
verses.text_big5_plain: 凡外腎損傷、或壓碎、或破裂、或割除的，不可獻給耶和華；在你們的地上不可這樣行。

verses.text_gb: 这类的牲畜，你们一样也不可从[Fn1]外人的手接受，作你们神的食物献上；因为这些都有损坏，有残疾，必不蒙悦纳。
verses.text_big5: 這類的牲畜，你們一樣也不可從[Fn1]外人的手接受，作你們神的食物獻上；因為這些都有損壞，有殘疾，必不蒙悅納。
verses.text_en: And from the hand of a foreigner you shall not present the food of your God from any of these, because their corruption is in them. There is a blemish in them; they shall not be accepted for you.
verses.text_gb_plain: 这类的牲畜，你们一样也不可从外人的手接受，作你们神的食物献上；因为这些都有损坏，有残疾，必不蒙悦纳。
verses.text_big5_plain: 這類的牲畜，你們一樣也不可從外人的手接受，作你們神的食物獻上；因為這些都有損壞，有殘疾，必不蒙悅納。

footnotes.zh: 外人之手所献的供物不蒙神悦纳，表征照着不信者的方式将基督献给神，必为神拒绝。
footnotes.zh_big5: 外人之手所獻的供物不蒙神悅納，表徵照著不信者的方式將基督獻給神，必為神拒絕。
footnotes.en: 22:25 1 foreigner The offering from the hand of a foreigner not being accepted by God signifies that the offering of Christ to God in a way that is according to the unbelievers will be rejected by God.

verses.text_gb: 耶和华对摩西说，
verses.text_big5: 耶和華對摩西說，
verses.text_en: Then Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.text_gb_plain: 耶和华对摩西说，
verses.text_big5_plain: 耶和華對摩西說，

verses.text_gb: 才生的公牛、绵羊或山羊，七天当跟着母；从[Fn1][Cra]第八天以后，可以当供物蒙悦纳，作为献给耶和华的火祭。
verses.text_big5: 纔生的公牛、綿羊或山羊，七天當跟著母；從[Fn1][Cra]第八天以後，可以當供物蒙悅納，作為獻給耶和華的火祭。
verses.text_en: When an ox or a sheep or a goat is born, it shall remain seven days with its mother; and from the eighth day and onward it shall be accepted for the offering of an offering by fire to Jehovah.
verses.text_gb_plain: 才生的公牛、绵羊或山羊，七天当跟着母；从第八天以后，可以当供物蒙悦纳，作为献给耶和华的火祭。
verses.text_big5_plain: 纔生的公牛、綿羊或山羊，七天當跟著母；從第八天以後，可以當供物蒙悅納，作為獻給耶和華的火祭。

footnotes.zh: 这表征我们对基督的经历必须长到复活(第八天，就是新的一周开始—约二十1)的程度，才能蒙神悦纳，献给祂作食物。这要求我们学习如何拒绝天然的生命，而在复活里凭神圣的生命而活(加二20)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 這表徵我們對基督的經歷必須長到復活（第八天，就是新的一週開始—約二十1）的程度，纔能蒙神悅納，獻給祂作食物。這要求我們學習如何拒絕天然的生命，而在復活裏憑神聖的生命而活。（加二20。）
footnotes.en: 22:27 1 eighth This signifies that our experience of Christ must grow to the level of resurrection (the eighth day, the beginning of a new week — John 20:1) before it will be accepted as an offering to God for His food. This requires us to learn how to reject our natural life and live by the divine life in resurrection (Gal. 2:20).

refs.text_gb: 你牛羊头生的，也要这样；七天当跟着母，第八天要归给我。
refs.text_big5: 你牛羊頭生的，也要這樣；七天當跟著母，第八天要歸給我。
refs.text_en: You shall do the same with your oxen and with your sheep. Seven days it shall be with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.

verses.text_gb: 无论是母牛或母羊，不可同日宰母和子。
verses.text_big5: 無論是母牛或母羊，不可同日宰母和子。
verses.text_en: But whether cow or sheep, you shall not slaughter both it and its young on one day.
verses.text_gb_plain: 无论是母牛或母羊，不可同日宰母和子。
verses.text_big5_plain: 無論是母牛或母羊，不可同日宰母和子。

verses.text_gb: 你们献感谢祭给耶和华，要献得可蒙悦纳。
verses.text_big5: 你們獻感謝祭給耶和華，要獻得可蒙悅納。
verses.text_en: And when you sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving to Jehovah, you shall sacrifice it so that you may be accepted.
verses.text_gb_plain: 你们献感谢祭给耶和华，要献得可蒙悦纳。
verses.text_big5_plain: 你們獻感謝祭給耶和華，要獻得可蒙悅納。

verses.text_gb: 要[Fn1][Cra]当天吃，一点不可留到[Crb]早晨；我是耶和华。
verses.text_big5: 要[Fn1][Cra]當天喫，一點不可留到[Crb]早晨；我是耶和華。
verses.text_en: On the same day it shall be eaten; you shall leave none of it until the morning; I am Jehovah.
verses.text_gb_plain: 要当天吃，一点不可留到早晨；我是耶和华。
verses.text_big5_plain: 要當天喫，一點不可留到早晨；我是耶和華。

footnotes.zh: 要当天吃感谢祭的祭牲(29)，一点不可留到早晨，表征我们献上基督作为对神的感谢，必须是新鲜的、全新的，一点不可留下以致变为陈旧(来十三15)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 要當天喫感謝祭的祭牲，（29，）一點不可留到早晨，表徵我們獻上基督作為對神的感謝，必須是新鮮的、全新的，一點不可留下以致變為陳舊。（來十三15。）
footnotes.en: 22:30 1 same Eating the sacrifice of thanksgiving (v. 29) on the same day and leaving none of it until the morning signify that our offering of Christ as a thanksgiving to God must be fresh and new, with nothing left to become stale (Heb. 13:15).

refs.text_gb: 这祭物要在献的当天或第二天吃，若有剩到第三天的，就要用火焚烧。
refs.text_big5: 這祭物要在獻的當天或第二天喫，若有剩到第三天的，就要用火焚燒。
refs.text_en: It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it, or on the next day, but what remains until the third day shall be burned with fire.

refs.text_gb: 若所献的供物是为还愿，或是甘心献的，要在献祭的日子吃，所剩下的第二天也可以吃。
refs.text_big5: 若所獻的供物是為還願，或是甘心獻的，要在獻祭的日子喫，所剩下的第二天也可以喫。
refs.text_en: But if the sacrifice of his offering is a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day that he presents his sacrifice, and on the next day what remains of it shall be eaten;

refs.text_gb: 他为感谢所献平安祭牲的肉，要在献的日子吃，一点不可留到早晨。
refs.text_big5: 他為感謝所獻平安祭牲的肉，要在獻的日子喫，一點不可留到早晨。
refs.text_en: And the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving shall be eaten on the day of his offering; he shall not leave any of it until the morning.

verses.text_gb: 你们要谨守遵行我的诫命；我是耶和华。
verses.text_big5: 你們要謹守遵行我的誡命；我是耶和華。
verses.text_en: Therefore you shall keep My commandments and do them; I am Jehovah.
verses.text_gb_plain: 你们要谨守遵行我的诫命；我是耶和华。
verses.text_big5_plain: 你們要謹守遵行我的誡命；我是耶和華。

verses.text_gb: 你们不可亵渎我的圣名，我要在以色列人中被尊为圣；我是使你们分别为圣的耶和华，
verses.text_big5: 你們不可褻瀆我的聖名，我要在以色列人中被尊為聖；我是使你們分別為聖的耶和華，
verses.text_en: And you shall not profane My holy name, but I will be sanctified among the children of Israel; I am Jehovah who sanctifies you,
verses.text_gb_plain: 你们不可亵渎我的圣名，我要在以色列人中被尊为圣；我是使你们分别为圣的耶和华，
verses.text_big5_plain: 你們不可褻瀆我的聖名，我要在以色列人中被尊為聖；我是使你們分別為聖的耶和華，

verses.text_gb: 把你们从埃及地领出来，作你们的[Cra]神；我是耶和华。
verses.text_big5: 把你們從埃及地領出來，作你們的[Cra]神；我是耶和華。
verses.text_en: Who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God; I am Jehovah.
verses.text_gb_plain: 把你们从埃及地领出来，作你们的神；我是耶和华。
verses.text_big5_plain: 把你們從埃及地領出來，作你們的神；我是耶和華。

refs.text_gb: 我要取你们归我作我的百姓，我也要作你们的神。你们要知道我是耶和华你们的神，是把你们从埃及人所加的重担下领出来的。
refs.text_big5: 我要取你們歸我作我的百姓，我也要作你們的神。你們要知道我是耶和華你們的神，是把你們從埃及人所加的重擔下領出來的。
refs.text_en: And I will take you to Myself as My people, and I will be your God; and you shall know that I am Jehovah your God, the One who brought you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.

verses.text_gb: 耶和华对摩西说，
verses.text_big5: 耶和華對摩西說，
verses.text_en: Then Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.text_gb_plain: 耶和华对摩西说，
verses.text_big5_plain: 耶和華對摩西說，

verses.text_gb: 你要对以色列人说，这些是我耶和华所定的[Fn1][Cra]节期，就是你们要宣告为圣[Fn2]会的节期。
verses.text_big5: 你要對以色列人說，這些是我耶和華所定的[Fn1][Cra]節期，就是你們要宣告為聖[Fn2]會的節期。
verses.text_en: Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them, As to the appointed feasts of Jehovah, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, these are My appointed feasts.
verses.text_gb_plain: 你要对以色列人说，这些是我耶和华所定的节期，就是你们要宣告为圣会的节期。
verses.text_big5_plain: 你要對以色列人說，這些是我耶和華所定的節期，就是你們要宣告為聖會的節期。

footnotes.zh: 节期乃是为着安息和享受，二者都是预表基督作我们的安息和享受。本书是一卷论到神的祭司体系，在与神的交通中事奉神的书，其中提到节期，指明我们作祭司对神的事奉，带进基督作我们与神之间，并我们彼此之间的安息与享受。神命定了节期，使祂的子民可以与祂一同安息，一同喜乐，使他们与神并彼此同享神为祂赎民所预备的一切。这享受和安息不是个人的，乃是团体的。
footnotes.zh_big5: 節期乃是為著安息和享受，二者都是豫表基督作我們的安息和享受。本書是一卷論到神的祭司體系，在與神的交通中事奉神的書，其中題到節期，指明我們作祭司對神的事奉，帶進基督作我們與神之間，並我們彼此之間的安息與享受。神命定了節期，使祂的子民可以與祂一同安息，一同喜樂，使他們與神並彼此同享神為祂贖民所豫備的一切。這享受和安息不是個人的，乃是團體的。
footnotes.en: 23:2 1 feasts The feasts are for rest and enjoyment, both of which are types of Christ as our rest and enjoyment. The mentioning of the feasts in this book, a book of God's priesthood for God's service in the fellowship of God, indicates that our priestly service to God issues in Christ as the rest and enjoyment that we have with God and with one another. God ordained the feasts that His people might rest with Him and be joyful with Him, that they might enjoy with Him and with one another all that He has provided for His redeemed people. The rest and enjoyment were not individual but corporate.

footnotes.zh: 耶和华所定的节期就是圣会，是神子民为着特别、专一目的而被召聚的特别聚集。这些圣会表征信徒聚集为召会(见弗一22注4)，在神面前，与神并彼此团体的以基督为安息和享受。
footnotes.zh_big5: 耶和華所定的節期就是聖會，是神子民為著特別、專一目的而被召聚的特別聚集。這些聖會表徵信徒聚集為召會，（見弗一22註4，）在神面前，與神並彼此團體的以基督為安息和享受。
footnotes.en: 23:2 2 convocations The feasts appointed by Jehovah were holy convocations, special assemblies of God's people called for a special and particular purpose. These signify the gathering of the believers as the church (see note Eph. 1:22 4 ) to have a corporate rest and enjoyment of Christ before God, with God, and with one another.

refs.text_gb: 一年三次，你要向我守节。
refs.text_big5: 一年三次，你要向我守節。
refs.text_en: Three times a year you shall hold a feast to Me.

refs.text_gb: 你要守除酵节，照我所吩咐你的，在亚笔月内所定的日期，吃无酵饼七天，因为你是在这月出埃及的。谁也不可空手朝见我。
refs.text_big5: 你要守除酵節，照我所吩咐你的，在亞筆月內所定的日期，喫無酵餅七天，因為你是在這月出埃及的。誰也不可空手朝見我。
refs.text_en: You shall keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread; as I commanded you, seven days you shall eat unleavened bread at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in it you came out from Egypt. And no one shall appear before Me empty.

refs.text_gb: 又要守收割节，所收割的是你田间所种、劳碌得来的初熟之物；也要在年底从田里收藏你劳碌得来之物时，守收藏节。
refs.text_big5: 又要守收割節，所收割的是你田間所種、勞碌得來的初熟之物；也要在年底從田裏收藏你勞碌得來之物時，守收藏節。
refs.text_en: And you shall keep the Feast of the Harvest, of the firstfruits of your labors from what you sow in the fruit of the field, and the Feast of Ingathering, at the end of the year when you gather in your labors out of the field.

refs.text_gb: 你所有的男丁，要一年三次朝见主耶和华。
refs.text_big5: 你所有的男丁，要一年三次朝見主耶和華。
refs.text_en: Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord Jehovah.

refs.text_gb: 耶和华所定的节期，就是你们到了所定的日期要宣告为圣会的，乃是这些：
refs.text_big5: 耶和華所定的節期，就是你們到了所定的日期要宣告為聖會的，乃是這些：
refs.text_en: These are the appointed feasts of Jehovah, even the holy convocations, which you shall proclaim at their appointed time:

refs.text_gb: 这些是耶和华所定的节期，就是你们要宣告为圣会的；要将火祭，就是燔祭和素祭，平安祭，并奠祭，各按各日献给耶和华。
refs.text_big5: 這些是耶和華所定的節期，就是你們要宣告為聖會的；要將火祭，就是燔祭和素祭，平安祭，並奠祭，各按各日獻給耶和華。
refs.text_en: These are the appointed feasts of Jehovah, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, to present an offering by fire to Jehovah, burnt offerings and meal offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings, each on its own day,

refs.text_gb: 这些祭要在你们所定的节期献给耶和华，都在所许的愿并甘心所献的以外，作为你们的燔祭、素祭、奠祭、和平安祭。
refs.text_big5: 這些祭要在你們所定的節期獻給耶和華，都在所許的願並甘心所獻的以外，作為你們的燔祭、素祭、奠祭、和平安祭。
refs.text_en: These you shall offer to Jehovah in your appointed feasts, besides your vows and your freewill offerings, for your burnt offerings and for your meal offerings and for your drink offerings and for your peace offerings.

verses.text_gb: [Cra]六日要作工，第七日是完全安息的[Fn1]安息日，当有圣会。你们什么工都不可作；这是在你们一切的住处向耶和华守的安息日。
verses.text_big5: [Cra]六日要作工，第七日是完全安息的[Fn1]安息日，當有聖會。你們甚麼工都不可作；這是在你們一切的住處向耶和華守的安息日。
verses.text_en: Six days work shall be done, but on the seventh day there is a Sabbath of complete rest, a holy convocation. You shall do no work; it is a Sabbath to Jehovah in all your dwelling places.
verses.text_gb_plain: 六日要作工，第七日是完全安息的安息日，当有圣会。你们什么工都不可作；这是在你们一切的住处向耶和华守的安息日。
verses.text_big5_plain: 六日要作工，第七日是完全安息的安息日，當有聖會。你們甚麼工都不可作；這是在你們一切的住處向耶和華守的安息日。

footnotes.zh: 每周的节期，安息日，表征蒙神救赎之人与神并彼此同享的安息。这安息日，这安息，乃是‘向耶和华守的’，表征神的赎民有分于使神喜乐并享受的安息。这也是每年七个节期中每个节期的主要意义(7～8，21，25，28，31～32，35～36，39)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 每週的節期，安息日，表徵蒙神救贖之人與神並彼此同享的安息。這安息日，這安息，乃是“向耶和華守的，”表徵神的贖民有分於使神喜樂並享受的安息。這也是每年七個節期中每個節期的主要意義。（7～8，21，25，28，31～32，35～36，39。）
footnotes.en: 23:3 1 Sabbath The weekly feast, the Sabbath, signifies the rest that God's redeemed people enjoy with God and with one another. This Sabbath, this rest, was “to Jehovah,” signifying a rest for God's joy and enjoyment, participated in by His redeemed people. This is also the principal denotation of each of the seven annual feasts (vv. 7-8, 21, 25, 28, 31-32, 35-36, 39).

refs.text_gb: 当记念安息日，将这日分别为圣。
refs.text_big5: 當記念安息日，將這日分別為聖。
refs.text_en: Remember the Sabbath day so as to sanctify it.

refs.text_gb: 六日要劳碌作你一切的工，
refs.text_big5: 六日要勞碌作你一切的工，
refs.text_en: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

refs.text_gb: 但第七日是向耶和华你神当守的安息日；这一日你和你的儿子、女儿、仆人、婢女、牲畜、并你城里的寄居者，无论何工都不可作；
refs.text_big5: 但第七日是向耶和華你神當守的安息日；這一日你和你的兒子、女兒、僕人、婢女、牲畜、並你城裏的寄居者，無論何工都不可作；
refs.text_en: But the seventh day is a Sabbath to Jehovah your God; you shall not do any work, you nor your son nor your daughter, your male servant nor your female servant, nor your cattle nor the sojourner with you, who is within your gates.

refs.text_gb: 因为六日之内，耶和华造天、地、海、和其中的万物，第七日便安息了；所以耶和华赐福与安息日，将这日分别为圣。
refs.text_big5: 因為六日之內，耶和華造天、地、海、和其中的萬物，第七日便安息了；所以耶和華賜福與安息日，將這日分別為聖。
refs.text_en: For in six days Jehovah made heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them, and rested on the seventh day; therefore Jehovah blessed the Sabbath day and sanctified it.

refs.text_gb: 六日你要作工，第七日要停工，使牛、驴可以歇息，并使你婢女的儿子和寄居的，都得以舒畅。
refs.text_big5: 六日你要作工，第七日要停工，使牛、驢可以歇息，並使你婢女的兒子和寄居的，都得以舒暢。
refs.text_en: Six days you shall do your work, and on the seventh day you shall cease from work so that your ox and your donkey may have rest, and the son of your female servant and the sojourner may be refreshed.

refs.text_gb: 六日要作工，但第七日是完全安息的安息日，是归耶和华为圣的；凡在安息日作工的，必要被处死。
refs.text_big5: 六日要作工，但第七日是完全安息的安息日，是歸耶和華為聖的；凡在安息日作工的，必要被處死。
refs.text_en: Six days work shall be done, but on the seventh day there is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to Jehovah; whoever does any work on the Sabbath day shall surely be put to death.

refs.text_gb: 你六日要作工，第七日要停工，虽在耕种和收割的时候，也要停工。
refs.text_big5: 你六日要作工，第七日要停工，雖在耕種和收割的時候，也要停工。
refs.text_en: Six days you shall work, but on the seventh day you shall cease from labor. Even in plowing time and in harvest time you shall cease from labor.

refs.text_gb: 六日要作工，但第七日你们要有完全安息的安息日，是归耶和华为圣的；凡在这日作工的，要被处死。
refs.text_big5: 六日要作工，但第七日你們要有完全安息的安息日，是歸耶和華為聖的；凡在這日作工的，要被處死。
refs.text_en: Six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day you shall have a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to Jehovah; whoever does any work on it shall be put to death.

refs.text_gb: 你们各人都当孝敬母亲和父亲，也要守我的安息日；我是耶和华你们的神。
refs.text_big5: 你們各人都當孝敬母親和父親，也要守我的安息日；我是耶和華你們的神。
refs.text_en: Each one of you shall fear his mother and his father, and you shall keep My Sabbaths; I am Jehovah your God.

refs.text_gb: 当照耶和华你神所吩咐的，守安息日，将这日分别为圣。
refs.text_big5: 當照耶和華你神所吩咐的，守安息日，將這日分別為聖。
refs.text_en: Keep the Sabbath day so as to sanctify it, as Jehovah your God has commanded you.

refs.text_gb: 六日要劳碌作你一切的工，
refs.text_big5: 六日要勞碌作你一切的工，
refs.text_en: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

refs.text_gb: 但第七日是向耶和华你神当守的安息日；这一日你和你的儿子、女儿、仆人、婢女、牛、驴、牲畜、并你城里的寄居者，无论何工都不可作，使你的仆人、婢女可以和你一样安息。
refs.text_big5: 但第七日是向耶和華你神當守的安息日；這一日你和你的兒子、女兒、僕人、婢女、牛、驢、牲畜、並你城裏的寄居者，無論何工都不可作，使你的僕人、婢女可以和你一樣安息。
refs.text_en: But the seventh day is a Sabbath to Jehovah your God; you shall not do any work, you nor your son nor your daughter nor your male servant nor your female servant nor your ox nor your donkey nor any of your cattle nor the sojourner with you who is within your gates, so that your male servant and your female servant may rest as you do.

refs.text_gb: 你要记念你在埃及地作过奴仆，耶和华你神用大能的手和伸出来的膀臂，将你从那里领出来；因此，耶和华你的神吩咐你守安息日。
refs.text_big5: 你要記念你在埃及地作過奴僕，耶和華你神用大能的手和伸出來的膀臂，將你從那裏領出來；因此，耶和華你的神吩咐你守安息日。
refs.text_en: And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt and that Jehovah your God brought you out from there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm; hence, Jehovah your God commanded you to hold the Sabbath day.

refs.text_gb: 管会堂的因为耶稣在安息日治病，就气忿忿地对群众说，有六日应当作工，在那六日之内，可以来求医，在安息日却不可。
refs.text_big5: 管會堂的因為耶穌在安息日治病，就氣忿忿的對群眾說，有六日應當作工，在那六日之內，可以來求醫，在安息日卻不可。
refs.text_en: But the ruler of the synagogue, being indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, answered and said to the crowd, There are six days in which man should work; therefore, come on them and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day.

footnotes.zh: 每年有七个节期。七是完全的数字，表征每年的七个节期乃是完全在神的丰富里。基督是安息日(3)的实际，也是每年一切节期的实际(西二16～17)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 每年有七個節期。七是完全的數字，表徵每年的七個節期乃是完全在神的豐富裏。基督是安息日（3）的實際，也是每年一切節期的實際。（西二16～17。）
footnotes.en: 23:4 1 feasts There were seven annual feasts. Seven is the number of fullness, signifying that the seven annual feasts were in the fullness of God's riches. Christ is the reality of the Sabbath (v. 3) and of all the annual feasts (Col. 2:16-17).

refs.text_gb: 一年三次，你要向我守节。
refs.text_big5: 一年三次，你要向我守節。
refs.text_en: Three times a year you shall hold a feast to Me.

refs.text_gb: 你要守除酵节，照我所吩咐你的，在亚笔月内所定的日期，吃无酵饼七天，因为你是在这月出埃及的。谁也不可空手朝见我。
refs.text_big5: 你要守除酵節，照我所吩咐你的，在亞筆月內所定的日期，喫無酵餅七天，因為你是在這月出埃及的。誰也不可空手朝見我。
refs.text_en: You shall keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread; as I commanded you, seven days you shall eat unleavened bread at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in it you came out from Egypt. And no one shall appear before Me empty.

refs.text_gb: 又要守收割节，所收割的是你田间所种、劳碌得来的初熟之物；也要在年底从田里收藏你劳碌得来之物时，守收藏节。
refs.text_big5: 又要守收割節，所收割的是你田間所種、勞碌得來的初熟之物；也要在年底從田裏收藏你勞碌得來之物時，守收藏節。
refs.text_en: And you shall keep the Feast of the Harvest, of the firstfruits of your labors from what you sow in the fruit of the field, and the Feast of Ingathering, at the end of the year when you gather in your labors out of the field.

refs.text_gb: 你所有的男丁，要一年三次朝见主耶和华。
refs.text_big5: 你所有的男丁，要一年三次朝見主耶和華。
refs.text_en: Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord Jehovah.

verses.text_gb: [Cra]正月十四日，[Fn1]黄昏的时候，是耶和华的[Fn2][Crb]逾越节。
verses.text_big5: [Cra]正月十四日，[Fn1]黃昏的時候，是耶和華的[Fn2][Crb]逾越節。
verses.text_en: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at twilight, is Jehovah's Passover,
verses.text_gb_plain: 正月十四日，黄昏的时候，是耶和华的逾越节。
verses.text_big5_plain: 正月十四日，黃昏的時候，是耶和華的逾越節。

footnotes.zh: 直译，两晚之间；大概指日落和黑夜之间的时间。
footnotes.zh_big5: 直譯，兩晚之間；大概指日落和黑夜之間的時間。
footnotes.en: 23:5 1 at Lit., between the two evenings; referring to the time interval between sunset and darkness.

footnotes.zh: 关于逾越节(5)和无酵节(6～8)，见出十二注。
footnotes.zh_big5: 關於逾越節（5）和無酵節，（6～8，）見出十二註。
footnotes.en: 23:5 2 Passover For the Feast of Passover (v. 5) and the Feast of Unleavened Bread (vv. 6-8), see notes in Exo. 12.

refs.text_gb: 从正月十四日晚上，直到二十一日晚上，你们要吃无酵饼。
refs.text_big5: 從正月十四日晚上，直到二十一日晚上，你們要喫無酵餅。
refs.text_en: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month in the evening, you shall eat unleavened bread, until the twenty-first day of the month in the evening.

refs.text_gb: 正月十四日是耶和华的逾越节。
refs.text_big5: 正月十四日是耶和華的逾越節。
refs.text_en: And in the first month on the fourteenth day of the month shall be Jehovah's Passover.

refs.text_gb: 这月十五日是节期，要吃无酵饼七日。
refs.text_big5: 這月十五日是節期，要喫無酵餅七日。
refs.text_en: And on the fifteenth day of this month shall be a feast; seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten.

refs.text_gb: 正月十四日，你们要守逾越节，守节七日，要吃无酵饼。
refs.text_big5: 正月十四日，你們要守逾越節，守節七日，要喫無酵餅。
refs.text_en: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall have the Passover, a feast of seven days; unleavened bread shall be eaten.

refs.text_gb: 你们当这样吃羊羔：腰间束带，脚上穿鞋，手中拿杖，赶紧地吃；这是耶和华的逾越节。
refs.text_big5: 你們當這樣喫羊羔：腰間束帶，腳上穿鞋，手中拿杖，趕緊的喫；這是耶和華的逾越節。
refs.text_en: And this is how you shall eat it: with your loins girded, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and you shall eat it in haste. It is Jehovah's passover.

refs.text_gb: 于是，摩西召了以色列的众长老来，对他们说，你们要按着家取出羊羔，把这逾越节的羊羔宰了。
refs.text_big5: 於是，摩西召了以色列的眾長老來，對他們說，你們要按著家取出羊羔，把這逾越節的羊羔宰了。
refs.text_en: Then Moses called for all the elders of Israel and said to them, Draw out and take lambs according to your families, and slaughter the passover.

refs.text_gb: 拿一把牛膝草，蘸盆里的血，打一些在门楣上，和左右的门框上。你们谁也不可出自己的房门，直到早晨。
refs.text_big5: 拿一把牛膝草，蘸盆裏的血，打一些在門楣上，和左右的門框上。你們誰也不可出自己的房門，直到早晨。
refs.text_en: And you shall take a bunch of hyssop and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and you shall apply some of the blood that is in the basin to the lintel and to the two doorposts; and none of you shall go outside the entrance of his house until the morning.

refs.text_gb: 因为耶和华要巡行击杀埃及人；祂看见血在门楣上，和左右的门框上，就必越过那门，不许灭命的进你们的房屋，击杀你们。
refs.text_big5: 因為耶和華要巡行擊殺埃及人；祂看見血在門楣上，和左右的門框上，就必越過那門，不許滅命的進你們的房屋，擊殺你們。
refs.text_en: For Jehovah will pass through to smite the Egyptians; and when He sees the blood upon the lintel and on the two doorposts, Jehovah will pass over the entrance and will not allow the destroyer to come into your houses to smite you.

refs.text_gb: 你们要守这话，作为你们和你们子孙永远的定例。
refs.text_big5: 你們要守這話，作為你們和你們子孫永遠的定例。
refs.text_en: And you shall observe this matter as a statute for you and for your sons in perpetuity.

refs.text_gb: 日后，你们到了耶和华按着应许所赐给你们的那地，就要持守这事奉。
refs.text_big5: 日後，你們到了耶和華按著應許所賜給你們的那地，就要持守這事奉。
refs.text_en: And when you come to the land which Jehovah will give you, as He has promised, you shall observe this service.

refs.text_gb: 你们的儿女问你们说，这事奉是什么意思？
refs.text_big5: 你們的兒女問你們說，這事奉是甚麼意思？
refs.text_en: And when your children say to you, What do you mean by this service?

refs.text_gb: 你们就要说，这是献给耶和华逾越节的祭。当以色列人在埃及的时候，祂击杀埃及人，越过以色列人的房屋，救了我们各家。于是百姓低头敬拜。
refs.text_big5: 你們就要說，這是獻給耶和華逾越節的祭。當以色列人在埃及的時候，祂擊殺埃及人，越過以色列人的房屋，救了我們各家。於是百姓低頭敬拜。
refs.text_en: You shall say, It is the passover sacrifice to Jehovah, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt when He smote the Egyptians and delivered our houses. And the people bowed and worshipped.

refs.text_gb: 若有外人寄居在你们中间，愿向耶和华守逾越节，他所有的男子务要受割礼，然后才让他前来遵守，他也就像本地人一样；但未受割礼的人，都不可吃这羊羔。
refs.text_big5: 若有外人寄居在你們中間，願向耶和華守逾越節，他所有的男子務要受割禮，然後纔讓他前來遵守，他也就像本地人一樣；但未受割禮的人，都不可喫這羊羔。
refs.text_en: But if a stranger sojourns with you and will observe the Passover to Jehovah, let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near to observe it; and he will be like one who is a native of the land. But no uncircumcised person shall eat of it.

refs.text_gb: 以色列人应当在所定的日期守逾越节。
refs.text_big5: 以色列人應當在所定的日期守逾越節。
refs.text_en: Let the children of Israel keep the passover at its appointed time.

refs.text_gb: 本月十四日黄昏的时候，你们要在所定的日期守这节，要按这节的一切律例和一切典章而守。
refs.text_big5: 本月十四日黃昏的時候，你們要在所定的日期守這節，要按這節的一切律例和一切典章而守。
refs.text_en: On the fourteenth day of this month at twilight, you shall keep it at its appointed time; according to all its statutes and according to all its ordinances you shall keep it.

verses.text_gb: 这月十五日是向耶和华守的[Cra]无酵节；你们要吃无酵饼七日。
verses.text_big5: 這月十五日是向耶和華守的[Cra]無酵節；你們要喫無酵餅七日。
verses.text_en: And on the fifteenth day of this month is the Feast of Unleavened Bread to Jehovah; seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
verses.text_gb_plain: 这月十五日是向耶和华守的无酵节；你们要吃无酵饼七日。
verses.text_big5_plain: 這月十五日是向耶和華守的無酵節；你們要喫無酵餅七日。

refs.text_gb: 你们要守无酵节，因为正当这日，我把你们的军队从埃及地领出来。所以你们要守这日，作为世世代代永远的定例。
refs.text_big5: 你們要守無酵節，因為正當這日，我把你們的軍隊從埃及地領出來。所以你們要守這日，作為世世代代永遠的定例。
refs.text_en: And you shall keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread, for on this very day I have brought your armies out of the land of Egypt; therefore you shall keep this day throughout your generations as a perpetual statute.

refs.text_gb: 摩西对百姓说，你们要记念从埃及为奴之家出来的这日，因为耶和华用大能的手，将你们从这地方领出来；有酵的物都不可吃。
refs.text_big5: 摩西對百姓說，你們要記念從埃及為奴之家出來的這日，因為耶和華用大能的手，將你們從這地方領出來；有酵的物都不可喫。
refs.text_en: And Moses said to the people, Remember this day on which you came out from Egypt, from the slave house, for by strength of hand Jehovah brought you out from this place; and nothing leavened shall be eaten.

refs.text_gb: 你要吃无酵饼七日，到第七日要向耶和华守节。
refs.text_big5: 你要喫無酵餅七日，到第七日要向耶和華守節。
refs.text_en: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a feast to Jehovah.

refs.text_gb: 你要守除酵节，照我所吩咐你的，在亚笔月内所定的日期，吃无酵饼七天，因为你是在这月出埃及的。谁也不可空手朝见我。
refs.text_big5: 你要守除酵節，照我所吩咐你的，在亞筆月內所定的日期，喫無酵餅七天，因為你是在這月出埃及的。誰也不可空手朝見我。
refs.text_en: You shall keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread; as I commanded you, seven days you shall eat unleavened bread at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in it you came out from Egypt. And no one shall appear before Me empty.

refs.text_gb: 你要守除酵节，照我所吩咐你的，在亚笔月内所定的日期，吃无酵饼七天，因为你是在亚笔月内出埃及的。
refs.text_big5: 你要守除酵節，照我所吩咐你的，在亞筆月內所定的日期，喫無酵餅七天，因為你是在亞筆月內出埃及的。
refs.text_en: You shall keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in the month of Abib you came out from Egypt.

refs.text_gb: 这月十五日是节期，要吃无酵饼七日。
refs.text_big5: 這月十五日是節期，要喫無酵餅七日。
refs.text_en: And on the fifteenth day of this month shall be a feast; seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten.

verses.text_gb: [Fn1][Cra]第一日当有圣会，什么劳碌的工都不可作；
verses.text_big5: [Fn1][Cra]第一日當有聖會，甚麼勞碌的工都不可作；
verses.text_en: On the first day you shall have a holy convocation; you shall do no work of labor.
verses.text_gb_plain: 第一日当有圣会，什么劳碌的工都不可作；
verses.text_big5_plain: 第一日當有聖會，甚麼勞碌的工都不可作；

footnotes.zh: 无酵节的第一日和最后一日(8)有圣会，什么劳碌的工都不可作，表征在我们基督徒生活的期间，从头一天到最后一天，我们乃是团体的享受基督，并无人为的劳碌。
footnotes.zh_big5: 無酵節的第一日和最後一日（8）有聖會，甚麼勞碌的工都不可作，表徵在我們基督徒生活的期間，從頭一天到最後一天，我們乃是團體的享受基督，並無人為的勞碌。
footnotes.en: 23:7 1 first Having a holy convocation on the first day and on the last day (v. 8) of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, with no work of labor, signifies that we enjoy Christ corporately, without our human labor, from the first day until the last day of the course of our Christian life.

refs.text_gb: 第一日当有圣会；什么劳碌的工都不可作。
refs.text_big5: 第一日當有聖會；甚麼勞碌的工都不可作。
refs.text_en: On the first day there shall be a holy convocation; you shall do no work of labor;

refs.text_gb: 只要将公牛犊两只，公绵羊一只，一岁的公羊羔七只，都要你们看为没有残疾的，献为火祭，给耶和华为燔祭。
refs.text_big5: 只要將公牛犢兩隻，公綿羊一隻，一歲的公羊羔七隻，都要你們看為沒有殘疾的，獻為火祭，給耶和華為燔祭。
refs.text_en: But you shall present an offering by fire, a burnt offering to Jehovah: two bulls of the herd and one ram and seven male lambs a year old; they shall be without blemish for you;

refs.text_gb: 一连七日，每日要这样把怡爽香气之火祭的食物献给耶和华，要在常献的燔祭和同献的奠祭以外献上。
refs.text_big5: 一連七日，每日要這樣把怡爽香氣之火祭的食物獻給耶和華，要在常獻的燔祭和同獻的奠祭以外獻上。
refs.text_en: In this way you shall offer daily, for seven days, the food of the offering by fire, a satisfying fragrance to Jehovah; it shall be offered besides the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.

refs.text_gb: 第七日你们当有圣会，什么劳碌的工都不可作。
refs.text_big5: 第七日你們當有聖會，甚麼勞碌的工都不可作。
refs.text_en: And on the seventh day you shall have a holy convocation; you shall do no work of labor.

verses.text_gb: 要将火祭献给耶和华[Fn1]七日。第七日当有圣会，什么劳碌的工都不可作。
verses.text_big5: 要將火祭獻給耶和華[Fn1]七日。第七日當有聖會，甚麼勞碌的工都不可作。
verses.text_en: But you shall present an offering by fire to Jehovah seven days. On the seventh day there shall be a holy convocation; you shall do no work of labor.
verses.text_gb_plain: 要将火祭献给耶和华七日。第七日当有圣会，什么劳碌的工都不可作。
verses.text_big5_plain: 要將火祭獻給耶和華七日。第七日當有聖會，甚麼勞碌的工都不可作。

footnotes.zh: 将火祭献给耶和华七日(一段完全的期间)，表征我们在基督徒生活的整个期间，不断地把基督献给神作食物。在主的筵席上，我们向全宇宙展示，在一周里我们天天取用基督作我们无酵的食物，作我们生命的供应，而远离罪(林前五7～8)，并且我们是带着祂来赴席。然后我们将所享受为食物的这一位，献给神使祂满足。
footnotes.zh_big5: 將火祭獻給耶和華七日（一段完全的期間，）表徵我們在基督徒生活的整個期間，不斷的把基督獻給神作食物。在主的筵席上，我們向全宇宙展示，在一週裏我們天天取用基督作我們無酵的食物，作我們生命的供應，而遠離罪，（林前五7～8，）並且我們是帶著祂來赴席。然後我們將所享受為食物的這一位，獻給神使祂滿足。
footnotes.en: 23:8 1 seven The presenting of an offering by fire to Jehovah for seven days (a full course of time) signifies that we offer Christ as food to God continually through the full course of our Christian life. At the Lord's table we make a display to the entire universe that each day of the week we take Christ as our unleavened food, as our life supply apart from sin (1 Cor. 5:7-8), and that we come to the table with Him. Then we offer to God for His satisfaction the One whom we have been enjoying as our food.

verses.text_gb: 耶和华对摩西说，
verses.text_big5: 耶和華對摩西說，
verses.text_en: Then Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.text_gb_plain: 耶和华对摩西说，
verses.text_big5_plain: 耶和華對摩西說，

verses.text_gb: 你要对以色列人说，你们进了我赐给你们的地，收割庄稼的时候，要将[Fn1][Cra]初熟的庄稼一捆带给祭司；
verses.text_big5: 你要對以色列人說，你們進了我賜給你們的地，收割莊稼的時候，要將[Fn1][Cra]初熟的莊稼一捆帶給祭司；
verses.text_en: Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them, When you come into the land which I am giving you, and reap its harvest, then you shall bring the sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest to the priest;
verses.text_gb_plain: 你要对以色列人说，你们进了我赐给你们的地，收割庄稼的时候，要将初熟的庄稼一捆带给祭司；
verses.text_big5_plain: 你要對以色列人說，你們進了我賜給你們的地，收割莊稼的時候，要將初熟的莊稼一捆帶給祭司；

footnotes.zh: 每年第三个节期是初熟节，表征作初熟果子的复活基督(林前十五20)，在祂的复活里乃是给我们享受的筵席(见林前十五20注2与太二七53注1)。基督在逾越节时被钉十字架(可十四12与注2)，然后在第三天(林前十五4)，就是安息日的次日(11，约二十1)，祂复活了。基督的复活是初熟节的应验，也是这节期的实际。
footnotes.zh_big5: 每年第三個節期是初熟節，表徵作初熟果子的復活基督，（林前十五20，）在祂的復活裏乃是給我們享受的筵席。（見林前十五20註2與太二七53註1。）基督在逾越節時被釘十字架，（可十四12與註2，）然後在第三天，（林前十五4，）就是安息日的次日，（11，約二十1，）祂復活了。基督的復活是初熟節的應驗，也是這節期的實際。
footnotes.en: 23:10 1 sheaf The third annual feast, the Feast of Firstfruits, signifies the resurrected Christ as the firstfruits (1 Cor. 15:20) for our enjoyment as a feast in His resurrection (see note 1 Cor. 15:20 2 and note Matt. 27:53 1 ). Christ was crucified at the time of the Feast of the Passover (Mark 14:12 and note Mark 14:12 2 ), and then on the third day (1 Cor. 15:4), the day after the Sabbath (v. 11; John 20:1), He was resurrected. Christ's resurrection was the fulfillment of the Feast of Firstfruits and is the reality of that feast.

refs.text_gb: 地里首先初熟之物，要带到耶和华你神的殿中。不可用山羊羔母的奶煮山羊羔。

refs.text_en: The first of the firstfruits of your ground you shall bring to the house of Jehovah your God. You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk.

refs.text_en: From the first of your dough you shall offer up a cake for a heave offering; as the heave offering of the threshing floor, so shall you offer it up.

refs.text_gb: 你们世世代代要用初熟的麦子磨面，作为举祭献给耶和华。
refs.text_big5: 你們世世代代要用初熟的麥子磨麵，作為舉祭獻給耶和華。
refs.text_en: From the first of your dough you shall give to Jehovah a heave offering throughout your generations.

refs.text_en: Also in the day of the firstfruits, when you present a new meal offering to Jehovah in your Feast of Weeks, you shall have a holy convocation; you shall do no work of labor;

refs.text_gb: 你进去得了耶和华你神所赐你为业之地，住在那里，
refs.text_big5: 你進去得了耶和華你神所賜你為業之地，住在那裏，
refs.text_en: And when you enter the land which Jehovah your God is giving you as an inheritance, and you possess it and dwell in it,

refs.text_gb: 就要将地里各种初熟的出产，就是从耶和华你神赐你的地上所收的，取些来盛在筐子里，往耶和华你神所选择给祂名居住的地方去，
refs.text_big5: 就要將地裏各種初熟的出產，就是從耶和華你神賜你的地上所收的，取些來盛在筐子裏，往耶和華你神所選擇給祂名居住的地方去，
refs.text_en: You shall take some of the first of all the fruit of the ground which you shall bring from your land, which Jehovah your God is giving you, and you shall put it in a basket and go to the place where Jehovah your God will choose to cause His name to dwell.

refs.text_gb: 这些人未曾与妇女在一起受到玷污，他们原是童身。羔羊无论往哪里去，他们都跟随祂。他们是从人间买来的，作初熟的果子归与神和羔羊；
refs.text_big5: 這些人未曾與婦女在一起受到玷污，他們原是童身。羔羊無論往那裏去，他們都跟隨祂。他們是從人間買來的，作初熟的果子歸與神和羔羊；
refs.text_en: These are they who have not been defiled with women, for they are virgins. These are they who follow the Lamb wherever He may go. These were purchased from among men as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb.

verses.text_gb: 他要把这一捆在耶和华面前[Cra]摇一摇，使你们[Fn1]蒙悦纳；祭司要在[Crb]安息日的次日把这捆摇一摇。

verses.text_en: And he shall wave the sheaf before Jehovah for your acceptance; on the day after the Sabbath the priest shall wave it.

footnotes.en: 23:11 1 acceptance The waving of the sheaf of firstfruits before Jehovah for acceptance signifies that Christ was resurrected that we might be justified before God and accepted by God (Rom. 4:25b).

refs.text_en: And the priest shall wave them with the bread of the firstfruits as a wave offering before Jehovah with the two lambs; they shall be holy to Jehovah for the priest.

refs.text_en: Now late on the Sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, Mary the Magdalene and the other Mary came to look at the grave.

verses.text_gb: 摇这捆的日子，你们要把一只一岁、没有残疾的公绵羊羔献给耶和华为[Fn1][Cra]燔祭。
verses.text_big5: 搖這捆的日子，你們要把一隻一歲、沒有殘疾的公綿羊羔獻給耶和華為[Fn1][Cra]燔祭。
verses.text_en: And on the day when you wave the sheaf, you shall offer a male lamb a year old without blemish as a burnt offering to Jehovah.
verses.text_gb_plain: 摇这捆的日子，你们要把一只一岁、没有残疾的公绵羊羔献给耶和华为燔祭。
verses.text_big5_plain: 搖這捆的日子，你們要把一隻一歲、沒有殘疾的公綿羊羔獻給耶和華為燔祭。

footnotes.zh: 献摇祭的日子，把一只一岁、没有残疾的公绵羊羔献给耶和华为燔祭，表征复活的基督是新鲜、柔细、温和、刚强、毫无瑕疵的，献给神作燔祭，绝对的为着神。这供物不仅含示基督自己，也含示祂所有的信徒，就是在祂里面与祂一同复活的人(弗二6)。信徒在基督里并与基督一同献给神作燔祭，他们就能过绝对为着神的生活。
footnotes.zh_big5: 獻搖祭的日子，把一隻一歲、沒有殘疾的公綿羊羔獻給耶和華為燔祭，表徵復活的基督是新鮮、柔細、溫和、剛強、毫無瑕疵的，獻給神作燔祭，絕對的為著神。這供物不僅含示基督自己，也含示祂所有的信徒，就是在祂裏面與祂一同復活的人。（弗二6。）信徒在基督裏並與基督一同獻給神作燔祭，他們就能過絕對為著神的生活。
footnotes.en: 23:12 1 burnt The offering of a male lamb a year old without blemish as a burnt offering on the day of the wave offering signifies that the resurrected Christ, being fresh, tender, meek, strong, and without blemish, is offered to God as a burnt offering that is absolutely for God. This offering implies not only Christ Himself but also all His believers, who were resurrected in Him and with Him (Eph. 2:6). Having been offered to God as a burnt offering in Christ and with Christ, the believers may live a life that is absolutely for God.

refs.text_gb: 人的供物若以羊为燔祭，或绵羊或山羊，就要献上没有残疾的公羊。
refs.text_big5: 人的供物若以羊為燔祭，或綿羊或山羊，就要獻上沒有殘疾的公羊。
refs.text_en: And if his offering is from the flock, of the sheep or of the goats, for a burnt offering, he shall present it, a male without blemish.

verses.text_gb: 同献的[Fn1]素祭，是调油的细面一伊法的十分之二，作为怡爽香气的火祭，献给耶和华。同献的[Fn2][Cra]奠祭，是酒一欣的四分之一。
verses.text_big5: 同獻的[Fn1]素祭，是調油的細麵一伊法的十分之二，作為怡爽香氣的火祭，獻給耶和華。同獻的[Fn2][Cra]奠祭，是酒一欣的四分之一。
verses.text_en: And its meal offering shall be two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mingled with oil, an offering by fire to Jehovah for a satisfying fragrance. And its drink offering shall be of wine, a fourth of a hin.
verses.text_gb_plain: 同献的素祭，是调油的细面一伊法的十分之二，作为怡爽香气的火祭，献给耶和华。同献的奠祭，是酒一欣的四分之一。
verses.text_big5_plain: 同獻的素祭，是調油的細麵一伊法的十分之二，作為怡爽香氣的火祭，獻給耶和華。同獻的奠祭，是酒一欣的四分之一。

footnotes.zh: 这里的素祭，表征复活的基督作我们的素祭，调和着施膏的灵，在基督的复活里献给神作食物，作使神满足的香气。
footnotes.zh_big5: 這裏的素祭，表徵復活的基督作我們的素祭，調和著施膏的靈，在基督的復活裏獻給神作食物，作使神滿足的香氣。
footnotes.en: 23:13 1 meal The meal offering here signifies the resurrected Christ as our meal offering mingled with the anointing Spirit, offered to God as food in Christ's resurrection as a fragrance for God's satisfaction.

footnotes.zh: 一1～六7的五种基本祭，乃是预表基督为着我们之于神的各方面所是。奠祭乃是在基本祭之外附加的，浇奠在基本祭之上(民十五1～10，二八7～10)。在初熟节时与燔祭(12)和素祭同献的奠祭，表征复活的基督在祂属人的生命里绝对为神而活，并在十字架上被浇奠(赛五三12下，腓二5～8)，而在复活里献给神，作神的享受。参腓二17与注1，提后四6与注1。
footnotes.zh_big5: 一1～六7的五種基本祭，乃是豫表基督為著我們之於神的各方面所是。奠祭乃是在基本祭之外附加的，澆奠在基本祭之上。（民十五1～10，二八7～10。）在初熟節時與燔祭（12）和素祭同獻的奠祭，表徵復活的基督在祂屬人的生命裏絕對為神而活，並在十字架上被澆奠，（賽五三12下，腓二5～8，）而在復活裏獻給神，作神的享受。參腓二17與註1，提後四6與註1。
footnotes.en: 23:13 2 drink The five basic offerings in 1:1—6:7 are types of various aspects of what Christ is to God on our behalf. The drink offering was in addition to the basic offerings and was poured out on one of the basic offerings (Num. 15:1-10; 28:7-10). The drink offering offered with the burnt offering (v. 12) and the meal offering at the Feast of Firstfruits signifies the resurrected Christ in His human life (in His living absolutely for God and His being poured out on the cross — Isa. 53:12b; Phil. 2:5-8), offered to God in His resurrection for God's enjoyment. Cf. Phil. 2:17 and note Phil. 2:17 1 ; 2 Tim. 4:6 and note 2 Tim. 4:6 1 .

refs.text_en: And with the one lamb a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mingled with a fourth of a hin of beaten oil, and a fourth of a hin of wine for a drink offering.

footnotes.zh: 这表征复活的基督升到诸天之上，在祂复活里带着所有的果子一同献给神，作神的食物，先使神满足(约二十17与注1)；然后才成为人的供应，使人满足。
footnotes.zh_big5: 這表徵復活的基督升到諸天之上，在祂復活裏帶著所有的果子一同獻給神，作神的食物，先使神滿足；（約二十17與註1；）然後纔成為人的供應，使人滿足。
footnotes.en: 23:14 1 no This signifies that the resurrected Christ ascended to the heavens and was offered to God with all the fruit in His resurrection as God's food for God's satisfaction first (John 20:17 and note John 20:17 1 ); then, He became man's supply for man's satisfaction.

verses.text_big5_plain: 到第七個安息日的次日，共計五十天，再要將新素祭獻給耶和華。

footnotes.zh: 见徒二1与注。五旬节就是第五十天的节期，从安息日的次日，就是将摇祭的禾捆带给神的日子(11)算起，到第七个安息日的次日(15)。这表征基督的复活七倍的丰满，达到完全丰满的范围，为著作复活的见证，担负完全的责任，由五十这数字所表征(五十，由十乘五所组成，十表征丰满，五表征负责任)。 在新约里五旬节那天，三一神的终极完成—经过过程之三一神那包罗万有、赐生命、复合的灵，就是三一神的总和—浇灌在代表基督身体的一百二十位门徒身上。神经纶的灵这样的浇灌，结果产生了基督的身体，作那无限、个人基督的扩增、扩大，使祂成为宇宙、团体的基督(林前十二12～13)，就是经过过程并终极完成之三一神与祂所拣选并救赎之人的调和，终极完成于新耶路撒冷。
footnotes.zh_big5: 見徒二1與註。五旬節就是第五十天的節期，從安息日的次日，就是將搖祭的禾捆帶給神的日子（11）算起，到第七個安息日的次日。（15。）這表徵基督的復活七倍的豐滿，達到完全豐滿的範圍，為著作復活的見證，擔負完全的責任，由五十這數字所表徵。（五十，由十乘五所組成，十表徵豐滿，五表徵負責任。）ˍ在新約裏五旬節那天，三一神的終極完成—經過過程之三一神那包羅萬有、賜生命、複合的靈，就是三一神的總和—澆灌在代表基督身體的一百二十位門徒身上。神經綸的靈這樣的澆灌，結果產生了基督的身體，作那無限、個人基督的擴增、擴大，使祂成為宇宙、團體的基督，（林前十二12～13，）就是經過過程並終極完成之三一神與祂所揀選並救贖之人的調和，終極完成於新耶路撒冷。
footnotes.en: 23:16 1 fifty See Acts 2:1 and note. The Feast of Pentecost was the feast of the fiftieth day, counting from the day after the Sabbath, the day on which the sheaf of the wave offering was brought to God (v. 11), to the day after the seventh Sabbath (v. 15). This signifies the resurrection of Christ in its sevenfold fullness reaching the realm of the complete fullness, bearing the full responsibility, signified by the number fifty (composed of ten times five, ten signifying fullness and five, responsibility), for the testimony of resurrection. On the day of Pentecost in the New Testament, the consummation of the Triune God — the all-inclusive, life-giving, compound Spirit of the processed Triune God, who is the totality of the Triune God — was poured out upon the one hundred twenty disciples as representatives of the Body of Christ. As a result of such an outpouring of the economical Spirit of God, the Body of Christ came into existence as the increase, the enlargement, of the unlimited, individual Christ, making Him the universal, corporate Christ (1 Cor. 12:12-13), the mingling of the processed and consummated Triune God with His chosen and redeemed people, which will ultimately consummate in the New Jerusalem.

refs.text_gb: 五旬节那天到了，门徒都聚集在一处。
refs.text_big5: 五旬節那天到了，門徒都聚集在一處。
refs.text_en: And as the day of Pentecost was being fulfilled, they were all together in the same place.

refs.text_gb: 在七七节，庄稼初熟，你们献新素祭给耶和华的日子，当有圣会；什么劳碌的工都不可作。
refs.text_big5: 在七七節，莊稼初熟，你們獻新素祭給耶和華的日子，當有聖會；甚麼勞碌的工都不可作。
refs.text_en: Also in the day of the firstfruits, when you present a new meal offering to Jehovah in your Feast of Weeks, you shall have a holy convocation; you shall do no work of labor;

verses.text_gb: 要从你们的住处带来[Fn1]两个摇祭的饼，是用细面一伊法的十分之二加[Cra]酵烤成的，当作初熟之物献给耶和华。
verses.text_big5: 要從你們的住處帶來[Fn1]兩個搖祭的餅，是用細麵一伊法的十分之二加[Cra]酵烤成的，當作初熟之物獻給耶和華。
verses.text_en: You shall bring out of your dwelling places two loaves as a wave offering; they shall be of two tenths of an ephah of fine flour, baked with leaven, as firstfruits to Jehovah.
verses.text_gb_plain: 要从你们的住处带来两个摇祭的饼，是用细面一伊法的十分之二加酵烤成的，当作初熟之物献给耶和华。
verses.text_big5_plain: 要從你們的住處帶來兩個搖祭的餅，是用細麵一伊法的十分之二加酵烤成的，當作初熟之物獻給耶和華。

footnotes.zh: 献给耶和华的新素祭(16)，乃是加酵烤成的两个饼，当作初熟之物献给耶和华；这表征初熟果子(无酵细面)阶段的基督，在五旬节阶段，已经成为由两部分(两个饼—林前十17)组成之基督的身体—召会，献给神作新素祭，使神满足。其中一部分由犹太信徒所组成(徒二1～4)，另一部分由外邦信徒所组成(徒十34～38)；二者里面都有罪(由酵所表征。)(参徒五1～11，六1。) 这两个饼也是献给耶和华的初熟之物，指明不仅基督是初熟果子，召会也是初熟果子。作为细面的基督这初熟果子，乃是复活之日的初熟果子(林前十五20，约二十17)。至终，这细面在五旬节那天成了两个饼。按预表，这指明基督成为召会，召会是基督的扩大(约三29～30，林前十二12，西三10～11)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 獻給耶和華的新素祭，（16，）乃是加酵烤成的兩個餅，當作初熟之物獻給耶和華；這表徵初熟果子（無酵細麵）階段的基督，在五旬節階段，已經成為由兩部分（兩個餅—林前十17）組成之基督的身體—召會，獻給神作新素祭，使神滿足。其中一部分由猶太信徒所組成，（徒二1～4，）另一部分由外邦信徒所組成；（徒十34～38；）二者裏面都有罪（由酵所表徵。）（參徒五1～11，六1。）ˍ這兩個餅也是獻給耶和華的初熟之物，指明不僅基督是初熟果子，召會也是初熟果子。作為細麵的基督這初熟果子，乃是復活之日的初熟果子。（林前十五20，約二十17。）至終，這細麵在五旬節那天成了兩個餅。按豫表，這指明基督成為召會，召會是基督的擴大。（約三29～30，林前十二12，西三10～11。）
footnotes.en: 23:17 1 two The offering of a new meal offering to Jehovah (v. 16) of two loaves of bread baked with leaven as firstfruits to Jehovah signifies that Christ at the stage of the firstfruits (the unleavened fine flour) has become the church as the Body of Christ in two sections at the stage of Pentecost (the two loaves — 1 Cor. 10:17), offered to God as the new meal offering for God's satisfaction. One of the sections is composed of the Jewish believers (Acts 2:1-4) and the other, of the Gentile believers (Acts 10:34-48). Both sections had sins (signified by the leaven) within them (cf. Acts 5:1-11; 6:1). That the two loaves also were firstfruits to Jehovah indicates that not only Christ but also the church are the firstfruits. Christ the firstfruits, as the fine flour, was the firstfruits on the day of resurrection (1 Cor. 15:20; John 20:17). Eventually, this fine flour became the two loaves on the day of Pentecost. In type, this indicates that Christ has become the church, that the church is the enlargement of Christ (John 3:29-30; 1 Cor. 12:12; Col. 3:10-11).

refs.text_gb: 他要把这供物，与有酵的饼，和为感谢所献的平安祭，一同献上。
refs.text_big5: 他要把這供物，與有酵的餅，和為感謝所獻的平安祭，一同獻上。
refs.text_en: With cakes of leavened bread he shall present his offering with the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving.

verses.text_gb: 又要将没有残疾、一岁的羊羔七只、公牛犊一只、公绵羊两只，和饼一同奉上；这些与同献的[Fn1]素祭和奠祭要作为燔祭献给耶和华，就是作怡爽香气的火祭献给耶和华。
verses.text_big5: 又要將沒有殘疾、一歲的羊羔七隻、公牛犢一隻、公綿羊兩隻，和餅一同奉上；這些與同獻的[Fn1]素祭和奠祭要作為燔祭獻給耶和華，就是作怡爽香氣的火祭獻給耶和華。
verses.text_en: And you shall present with the bread seven lambs, a year old without blemish, and one bull of the herd and two rams; they shall be a burnt offering to Jehovah with their meal offering and their drink offerings, an offering by fire for a satisfying fragrance to Jehovah.
verses.text_gb_plain: 又要将没有残疾、一岁的羊羔七只、公牛犊一只、公绵羊两只，和饼一同奉上；这些与同献的素祭和奠祭要作为燔祭献给耶和华，就是作怡爽香气的火祭献给耶和华。
verses.text_big5_plain: 又要將沒有殘疾、一歲的羊羔七隻、公牛犢一隻、公綿羊兩隻，和餅一同奉上；這些與同獻的素祭和奠祭要作為燔祭獻給耶和華，就是作怡爽香氣的火祭獻給耶和華。

footnotes.zh: 将燔祭、素祭、奠祭和饼一同奉上，表征五旬节那天的召会是团体人，献给神作燔祭，绝对为神而活；其生活犹如素祭搀酵(罪)，又如奠祭(借殉道而为神倾倒性命—腓二17，提后四6)，借着被销毁，成为蒙神悦纳的火祭，使神与人都得满足。
footnotes.en: 23:18 1 burnt The presenting of the burnt offering, the meal offering, and the drink offering with the bread signifies that the church on the day of Pentecost was a corporate man offered to God as a burnt offering to live absolutely for God, with a living as a meal offering mixed with leaven — sins — and as a drink offering (pouring out its life for God by being martyred — Phil. 2:17; 2 Tim. 4:6) to be an offering by fire accepted by God by being consumed for the satisfaction of both God and man.

verses.text_gb: 你们要献一只公山羊作[Fn1]赎罪祭，两只一岁的公绵羊羔作平安祭。
verses.text_big5: 你們要獻一隻公山羊作[Fn1]贖罪祭，兩隻一歲的公綿羊羔作平安祭。
verses.text_en: And you shall offer one male goat for a sin offering and two male lambs, a year old, for a sacrifice of peace offerings.
verses.text_gb_plain: 你们要献一只公山羊作赎罪祭，两只一岁的公绵羊羔作平安祭。
verses.text_big5_plain: 你們要獻一隻公山羊作贖罪祭，兩隻一歲的公綿羊羔作平安祭。

footnotes.zh: 将赎罪祭和平安祭连同饼当作摇祭(20)献上，表征五旬节那天召会因为有罪(参徒五1～11)，需要基督作赎罪祭，又因人与神、人与人之间交通的缘故，也需要基督作平安祭。同时召会也享受基督作摇祭，就是复活(摇一摇)献给神，作召会享受的一位。
footnotes.en: 23:19 1 sin The offering of the sin offering and the peace offering as a wave offering (v. 20) with the bread signifies that because of its sins (cf. Acts 5:1-11), the church on the day of Pentecost needed Christ as its sin offering, and for the sake of the fellowship of man with God and man with man, it needed Christ as its peace offering. At the same time, it enjoyed Christ as its wave offering, as the One resurrected (waved) to God for the church's enjoyment.

verses.text_gb: 祭司要把这些和初熟之物作的饼，连同两只公绵羊羔，一同作摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇；这些是归耶和华为圣，给与祭司的。
verses.text_big5: 祭司要把這些和初熟之物作的餅，連同兩隻公綿羊羔，一同作搖祭，在耶和華面前搖一搖；這些是歸耶和華為聖，給與祭司的。
verses.text_en: And the priest shall wave them with the bread of the firstfruits as a wave offering before Jehovah with the two lambs; they shall be holy to Jehovah for the priest.
verses.text_gb_plain: 祭司要把这些和初熟之物作的饼，连同两只公绵羊羔，一同作摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇；这些是归耶和华为圣，给与祭司的。
verses.text_big5_plain: 祭司要把這些和初熟之物作的餅，連同兩隻公綿羊羔，一同作搖祭，在耶和華面前搖一搖；這些是歸耶和華為聖，給與祭司的。

verses.text_gb: 当这日，你们要宣告有圣会；[Fn1]什么劳碌的工都不可作。这在你们一切的住处，要作世世代代永远的定例。
verses.text_big5: 當這日，你們要宣告有聖會；[Fn1]甚麼勞碌的工都不可作。這在你們一切的住處，要作世世代代永遠的定例。
verses.text_en: And you shall make a proclamation on that same day; you shall have a holy convocation; you shall do no work of labor. It shall be a perpetual statute in all your dwelling places throughout your generations.
verses.text_gb_plain: 当这日，你们要宣告有圣会；什么劳碌的工都不可作。这在你们一切的住处，要作世世代代永远的定例。
verses.text_big5_plain: 當這日，你們要宣告有聖會；甚麼勞碌的工都不可作。這在你們一切的住處，要作世世代代永遠的定例。

footnotes.zh: 这表征蒙神救赎的人，就是召会，与神一同享受基督，不需要人的劳碌加添什么。
footnotes.zh_big5: 這表徵蒙神救贖的人，就是召會，與神一同享受基督，不需要人的勞碌加添甚麼。
footnotes.en: 23:21 1 no This signifies God's redeemed people as the church enjoying Christ with God without any need of human labor to add anything.

verses.text_gb: 你们收割地的庄稼时，不可割尽田角，也不可[Cra]拾取收割时所遗落的，要留给[Fn1]穷人和寄居的；我是耶和华你们的神。
verses.text_big5: 你們收割地的莊稼時，不可割盡田角，也不可[Cra]拾取收割時所遺落的，要留給[Fn1]窮人和寄居的；我是耶和華你們的神。
verses.text_en: And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not completely reap the corners of your field, nor shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest; you shall leave them for the poor and for the sojourner; I am Jehovah your God.
verses.text_gb_plain: 你们收割地的庄稼时，不可割尽田角，也不可拾取收割时所遗落的，要留给穷人和寄居的；我是耶和华你们的神。
verses.text_big5_plain: 你們收割地的莊稼時，不可割盡田角，也不可拾取收割時所遺落的，要留給窮人和寄居的；我是耶和華你們的神。

footnotes.zh: 田角的庄稼要留下，收割时所遗落的要留给穷人和寄居的，这表征在五旬节时，基督在祂复活里的恩典，还有余剩，使外邦人得以有分。见得二2～3与注，参太十五21～28与注。
footnotes.en: 23:22 1 poor The harvest remaining at the corners of the fields and the gleanings being left for the poor and the sojourners signify that the grace of Christ in His resurrection at the Feast of Pentecost has a remainder in which the Gentiles may participate. See Ruth 2:2-3 and notes; cf. Matt. 15:21-28 and notes.

refs.text_gb: 你们收割地的庄稼时，不可割尽田角，也不可拾取收割时所遗落的。
refs.text_big5: 你們收割地的莊稼時，不可割盡田角，也不可拾取收割時所遺落的。
refs.text_en: And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the corners of your field, nor shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest.

refs.text_gb: 不可摘尽葡萄园的果子，也不可拾取葡萄园所掉的果子，要留给穷人和寄居的；我是耶和华你们的神。
refs.text_big5: 不可摘盡葡萄園的果子，也不可拾取葡萄園所掉的果子，要留給窮人和寄居的；我是耶和華你們的神。
refs.text_en: And you shall not glean your vineyard nor shall you gather the fallen fruit of your vineyard. You shall leave them for the poor and for the sojourner; I am Jehovah your God.

refs.text_gb: 你在田间收割庄稼，若忘下一捆在田里，不可回去拾取，要留给寄居的与孤儿寡妇；这样，耶和华你神必在你手所办的一切事上，赐福与你。
refs.text_big5: 你在田間收割莊稼，若忘下一捆在田裏，不可回去拾取，要留給寄居的與孤兒寡婦；這樣，耶和華你神必在你手所辦的一切事上，賜福與你。
refs.text_en: When you reap your harvest in your field and you forget a sheaf in the field, you shall not turn back to gather it; it shall be for the sojourner, the orphan, and the widow, in order that Jehovah your God may bless you in all your undertakings.

refs.text_gb: 摩押女子路得对拿俄米说，请你让我往田间去，我在谁的眼中蒙恩，就在谁的身后拾取麦穗。拿俄米说，女儿啊，你只管去。
refs.text_big5: 摩押女子路得對拿俄米說，請你讓我往田間去，我在誰的眼中蒙恩，就在誰的身後拾取麥穗。拿俄米說，女兒阿，你只管去。
refs.text_en: And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, Let me go to the field and glean among the ears of grain after him in whose sight I find favor. And she said to her, Go, my daughter.

refs.text_gb: 路得就去了。她来到田间，在收割的人身后拾取麦穗，恰巧是在以利米勒家族的人波阿斯那块田里。
refs.text_big5: 路得就去了。她來到田間，在收割的人身後拾取麥穗，恰巧是在以利米勒家族的人波阿斯那塊田裏。
refs.text_en: So she went. And she came and gleaned in the field after the reapers; and she happened to glean in a portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was from Elimelech's family.

refs.text_gb: 她说，请你让我在收割的人身后，拾取打捆剩下的麦穗。她早晨就来了，直到如今，除了在屋子里坐一会儿，一直留在这里。
refs.text_big5: 她說，請你讓我在收割的人身後，拾取打捆剩下的麥穗。她早晨就來了，直到如今，除了在屋子裏坐一會兒，一直留在這裏。
refs.text_en: And she said, Let me glean and gather after the reapers among the sheaves. So she has come and continued since morning until now, and she has sat in the house for only a little while.

refs.text_gb: 这样，路得在田间拾取麦穗，直到晚上；将所拾取的打了，约有一伊法大麦。
refs.text_big5: 這樣，路得在田間拾取麥穗，直到晚上；將所拾取的打了，約有一伊法大麥。
refs.text_en: So she gleaned in the field until evening. And she beat out what she had gleaned, and it was about an ephah of barley.

verses.text_gb: 耶和华对摩西说，
verses.text_big5: 耶和華對摩西說，
verses.text_en: Then Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.text_gb_plain: 耶和华对摩西说，
verses.text_big5_plain: 耶和華對摩西說，

verses.text_gb: 你要对以色列人说，[Cra]七月初一日，你们要有完全的安息，要[Fn1][Crb]吹角作记念，当有圣会。
verses.text_big5: 你要對以色列人說，[Cra]七月初一日，你們要有完全的安息，要[Fn1][Crb]吹角作記念，當有聖會。
verses.text_en: Speak to the children of Israel, saying, In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a complete rest, a memorial commemorated by the blowing of trumpets, a holy convocation.
verses.text_gb_plain: 你要对以色列人说，七月初一日，你们要有完全的安息，要吹角作记念，当有圣会。
verses.text_big5_plain: 你要對以色列人說，七月初一日，你們要有完全的安息，要吹角作記念，當有聖會。

footnotes.zh: 吹角节，表征神召聚祂四散的子民(分散的以色列人)，并提醒他们，祂要向他们发出这样的呼召(太二四31，参赛二七13，诗八一3)。这节是在七月初一日，就是下半年的开始，表征神救赎的另一半，要成就在以色列人身上；神救赎的前一半，已经成就在召会身上。五旬节和吹角节之间的时间，表征召会时代，就是奥秘时代，从五旬节召会产生的那日起，一直持续到主回来，那时神要召聚四散的犹太人，归回他们列祖之地。神呼召祂的子民从分散中一同归回，使他们有圣会，表征他们转向神(悔改)，成为团体的子民。这对神所召聚的子民是记念和安息，他们在其中能将基督当作食物献给神，使神与人同得满足(25)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 吹角節，表徵神召聚祂四散的子民（分散的以色列人，）並題醒他們，祂要向他們發出這樣的呼召。（太二四31，參賽二七13，詩八一3。）這節是在七月初一日，就是下半年的開始，表徵神救贖的另一半，要成就在以色列人身上；神救贖的前一半，已經成就在召會身上。五旬節和吹角節之間的時間，表徵召會時代，就是奧祕時代，從五旬節召會產生的那日起，一直持續到主回來，那時神要召聚四散的猶太人，歸回他們列祖之地。神呼召祂的子民從分散中一同歸回，使他們有聖會，表徵他們轉向神（悔改，）成為團體的子民。這對神所召聚的子民是記念和安息，他們在其中能將基督當作食物獻給神，使神與人同得滿足。（25。）
footnotes.en: 23:24 1 blowing The Feast of the Blowing of Trumpets signifies God's calling together of His scattered people (the dispersed Israelites) and His reminding them that He will issue such a call to them (Matt. 24:31; cf. Isa. 27:13; Psa. 81:3). This feast was on the first day of the seventh month, the beginning of the second half of the year, signifying the second half of God's redemption, which is to be accomplished on Israel, the first half having been accomplished on the church. The interval between the Feast of Pentecost and the Feast of the Blowing of Trumpets signifies the church age, the age of mystery, which lasts from the day of Pentecost, when the church came into being, until the Lord's coming back, when God will call the scattered Jews to come back to the land of their fathers. God's calling His people back together from their dispersion will cause them to have a holy convocation, signifying their returning to God (repentance) and becoming a corporate people. This will be a memorial and a rest to God's gathered people, in which they will be able to offer Christ to God as food for the satisfaction of both God and man (v. 25).

footnotes.zh: 就属灵一面说，吹角表征宣扬福音，呼召罪人悔改得救(参二五9注1)；遮罪表征基督的救赎(见十六1注1)。遮罪节紧接在与以色列人悔改归向神有关的吹角节之后，这表征人得蒙救赎之日，是接在吹福音的角，并人对这角声所回应的悔改之后。遮罪日有双重的应用。按属灵意义，这节已经应用于新约信徒；按字面意义，这节将来要应用于犹太人。
footnotes.zh_big5: 就屬靈一面說，吹角表徵宣揚福音，呼召罪人悔改得救；（參二五9註1；）遮罪表徵基督的救贖。（見十六1註1。）遮罪節緊接在與以色列人悔改歸向神有關的吹角節之後，這表徵人得蒙救贖之日，是接在吹福音的角，並人對這角聲所回應的悔改之後。遮罪日有雙重的應用。按屬靈意義，這節已經應用於新約信徒；按字面意義，這節將來要應用於猶太人。
footnotes.en: 23:27 1 Expiation Spiritually, the blowing of the trumpets signifies the proclaiming of the gospel to call sinners to repentance and salvation (cf. note Lev. 25:9 1 ), and the expiation signifies Christ's redemption (see note Lev. 16:1 1 ). The Feast of Expiation closely followed the Feast of the Blowing of Trumpets, which involves Israel's repentance and return to God. This signifies that the day of man's redemption follows the trumpeting of the gospel and man's repentance as a reaction to it. The Feast of Expiation has a double application. Spiritually, this feast has been applied to the New Testament believers, and literally it will be applied in the future to the Jews.

footnotes.zh: 百姓刻苦己心，将火祭献给耶和华(27下，29)，表征忧伤痛悔，为罪伤痛，并将基督当作食物献给神，使神与人同得满足。这就是主耶稣回来时，犹太人所要作的(亚十二10～14，太二四30，启一7)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 百姓刻苦己心，將火祭獻給耶和華，（27下，29，）表徵憂傷痛悔，為罪傷痛，並將基督當作食物獻給神，使神與人同得滿足。這就是主耶穌回來時，猶太人所要作的。（亞十二10～14，太二四30，啟一7。）
footnotes.en: 23:27 2 afflict The people's afflicting their souls and bringing an offering by fire to Jehovah (vv. 27, 29) signify their mourning, repenting, and feeling sorrowful for sin, and offering Christ as food to God for the satisfaction of both God and man. This is what the Jews will do when the Lord Jesus comes back (Zech. 12:10-14; Matt. 24:30; Rev. 1:7).

footnotes.zh: 七日之久要将火祭献给耶和华，表征天天将基督当作食物献给神，使神与人同得满足。按照这预表，在千年国里每天都要献祭给神，表征在我们的经历中，基督乃是神的食物，献给神使神满足，我们也可以与神彼此享受安息。
footnotes.zh_big5: 七日之久要將火祭獻給耶和華，表徵天天將基督當作食物獻給神，使神與人同得滿足。按照這豫表，在千年國裏每天都要獻祭給神，表徵在我們的經歷中，基督乃是神的食物，獻給神使神滿足，我們也可以與神彼此享受安息。
footnotes.en: 23:36 1 Seven The presenting of an offering by fire to Jehovah for seven days signifies the offering of Christ day after day as food to God for the satisfaction of both God and man. According to this type, in the millennium every day an offering will be presented to God to signify that Christ is God's food in our experiences, which is offered to God for His satisfaction so that we and God may enjoy mutual rest.

footnotes.zh: 这表征神的子民乃是圣会众，将复活(由第八日所表征—约二十1)的基督当作食物献给神，使神与人同得满足；他们不需要作什么，只要安息。这指明整个千年国的一千年，将是神与祂赎民的安息。见来四9注1。
footnotes.zh_big5: 這表徵神的子民乃是聖會眾，將復活（由第八日所表徵—約二十1）的基督當作食物獻給神，使神與人同得滿足；他們不需要作甚麼，只要安息。這指明整個千年國的一千年，將是神與祂贖民的安息。見來四9註1。
footnotes.en: 23:36 2 eighth This signifies that God's people as a sacred congregation offer Christ in resurrection (signified by the eighth day — John 20:1) as food to God for the satisfaction of both God and man, not needing to do any work but resting. This indicates that the entire one thousand years of the millennium will be a rest for God and for God's redeemed people. See note Heb. 4:9 1 .

refs.text_big5: 第八日你們當有嚴肅會；甚麼勞碌的工都不可作；
refs.text_en: On the eighth day you shall have a solemn assembly; you shall do no work of labor,

verses.text_gb: 这些是耶和华所定的节期，就是你们要宣告为圣会的；要将火祭，就是燔祭和素祭，平安祭，并奠祭，各按各日献给耶和华。

verses.text_gb_plain: 这些是耶和华所定的节期，就是你们要宣告为圣会的；要将火祭，就是燔祭和素祭，平安祭，并奠祭，各按各日献给耶和华。

verses.text_en: Besides the Sabbaths of Jehovah and besides your gifts and besides all your vows and besides all your freewill offerings which you give to Jehovah.

verses.text_en: Then on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the produce of the land, you shall keep the feast of Jehovah seven days; on the first day shall be a complete rest, and on the eighth day shall be a complete rest.
verses.text_gb_plain: 你们收藏了地的出产，从七月十五日起，要守耶和华的节七日；第一日要有完全的安息，第八日也要有完全的安息。

footnotes.zh: 这表征神收割了祂在地上所渴望得着的之后，千年国就要来临；这要经过千年国以前的三个时代—法前时代(从亚当到摩西—罗五14)、律法时代(从摩西到基督第一次来—约一17)、以及召会时代(从五旬节到基督第二次来—徒一11。)千年国，就是国度时代(启二十4，6)，将是旧天旧地的第四个，也是最后一个时代，要引进新天新地和新耶路撒冷，直到永远(启二一1～3)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 這表徵神收割了祂在地上所渴望得著的之後，千年國就要來臨；這要經過千年國以前的三個時代—法前時代（從亞當到摩西—羅五14、）律法時代（從摩西到基督第一次來—約一17、）以及召會時代（從五旬節到基督第二次來—徒一11。）千年國，就是國度時代，（啟二十4，6，）將是舊天舊地的第四個，也是最後一個時代，要引進新天新地和新耶路撒冷，直到永遠。（啟二一1～3。）
footnotes.en: 23:39 1 gathered This signifies that the millennium will come after the harvest of what God desires to obtain on earth through the three dispensations before the millennium — the dispensation before the law (from Adam to Moses — Rom. 5:14), the dispensation of the law (from Moses to Christ's first coming — John 1:17), and the dispensation of the church (from Pentecost to Christ's second coming — Acts 1:11). The millennium, the age of the kingdom (Rev. 20:4, 6), will be the fourth and final dispensation of the old heaven and the old earth. It will usher in the new heaven and new earth with the New Jerusalem for eternity (Rev. 21:1-3).

footnotes.en: 23:42 1 booths The coming millennium will be a conclusion of all that God has done with His redeemed people in the full course of the ages, the dispensations, in His old creation. The people dwelling in booths indicates that in the four dispensations of the old creation man cannot have a solid dwelling place. Eventually, for God's redeemed people the present, portable tabernacles will become a solid one — the New Jerusalem with twelve foundations (Heb. 11:8-10; Rev. 21:2-3, 14). See note John 7:2 1 , par. 3.

footnotes.zh: 本章的七个节期分为两组，第一组有四个，第二组有三个。第一组的四个节期都是在上半年，表征基督受死、复活以及升天将圣灵浇灌下来的时候。第二组的三个节期是在每年的七月，表征基督再来的时候。按照其时代的应验，头四个已经发生，后三个将来要发生。逾越节已经应验于基督受死之日(太二六2，17～19，26～28，林前五7)。无酵节正应验于召会时代(林前五7～8)。初熟节已经应验于基督复活之日(林前十五20)，那时产生了基督的肢体，以形成召会(彼前一3，弗二6)。五旬节已经应验于基督复活后五十天，就是圣灵浇灌下来之日(徒二1～4，参徒一3)，那时复活并升天的基督作为终极完成、包罗万有、赐生命的灵，把祂自己浇灌在祂的肢体上，以形成召会。吹角节将要应验于基督再来时(太二四31)。遮罪节要应验于以色列人被聚集回到他们列祖之地，回转归向神的日子(罗十一26～27，亚十二10～14)。住棚节要应验于要来的千年国，为期一千年(启二十4～6)，是神旧造一切时期的总结，为着要来的新天新地，以新耶路撒冷为其中心(启二一1～2)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 本章的七個節期分為兩組，第一組有四個，第二組有三個。第一組的四個節期都是在上半年，表徵基督受死、復活、以及升天將聖靈澆灌下來的時候。第二組的三個節期是在每年的七月，表徵基督再來的時候。按照其時代的應驗，頭四個已經發生，後三個將來要發生。逾越節已經應驗於基督受死之日。（太二六2，17～19，26～28，林前五7。）無酵節正應驗於召會時代。（林前五7～8。）初熟節已經應驗於基督復活之日，（林前十五20，）那時產生了基督的肢體，以形成召會。（彼前一3，弗二6。）五旬節已經應驗於基督復活後五十天，就是聖靈澆灌下來之日，（徒二1～4，參徒一3，）那時復活並升天的基督作為終極完成、包羅萬有、賜生命的靈，把祂自己澆灌在祂的肢體上，以形成召會。吹角節將要應驗於基督再來時。（太二四31。）遮罪節要應驗於以色列人被聚集回到他們列祖之地，回轉歸向神的日子。（羅十一26～27，亞十二10～14。）住棚節要應驗於要來的千年國，為期一千年，（啟二十4～6，）是神舊造一切時期的總結，為著要來的新天新地，以新耶路撒冷為其中心。（啟二一1～2。）
footnotes.en: 23:44 1 feasts The seven feasts in this chapter are in two groups, with four in the first group and three in the second. The four feasts in the first group all took place in the first half of the year, signifying the time when Christ died, resurrected, and ascended to pour out the Holy Spirit. The three feasts in the second group took place in the seventh month of the year, signifying the time of Christ's second coming. According to their dispensational fulfillment, the first four have taken place already, and the last three will take place in the future. The Feast of the Passover was fulfilled on the day of Christ's death (Matt. 26:2, 17-19, 26-28; 1 Cor. 5:7). The Feast of Unleavened Bread is being fulfilled in the church age (1 Cor. 5:7-8). The Feast of Firstfruits was fulfilled on the day of Christ's resurrection (1 Cor. 15:20), when the members of Christ were produced for the formation of the church (1 Pet. 1:3; Eph. 2:6). The Feast of Pentecost was fulfilled fifty days after Christ's resurrection, on the day of the pouring out of the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:1-4; cf. Acts 1:3), when the resurrected and ascended Christ as the consummated, all-inclusive, life-giving Spirit poured Himself out on His members to form the church. The Feast of the Blowing of Trumpets will be fulfilled at Christ's second coming (Matt. 24:31). The Feast of Expiation will be fulfilled on the day of Israel's return to God, after they have been gathered back to their fathers' land (Rom. 11:26-27; Zech. 12:10-14). The Feast of Tabernacles will be fulfilled in the coming millennium for a thousand years (Rev. 20:4-6) as a conclusion of all the ages of God's old creation, for the coming of the new heaven and the new earth with the New Jerusalem as their center (Rev. 21:1-2).

footnotes.zh_big5: 1～9節揭示，我們這些神的聖民要過聖別的生活，就需要有更新的安排，讓基督作神聖的光照耀我們，並作神聖的食物餧養我們。
footnotes.en: 24:1 1 saying Verses Lev. 24:1-9 unveil that for us, the holy people of God, to live a holy life, we need the arranging afresh of Christ as the divine light to shine over us and as the divine food to nourish us.

verses.text_gb: [Cra]你要吩咐以色列人，把[Fn1]捣成的纯橄榄油拿来给你，为点灯用，[Fn2]使灯常常点着。
verses.text_big5: [Cra]你要吩咐以色列人，把[Fn1]搗成的純橄欖油拿來給你，為點燈用，[Fn2]使燈常常點著。
verses.text_en: Command the children of Israel to bring to you pure oil of beaten olives for the light, to make the lamps burn continually.
verses.text_gb_plain: 你要吩咐以色列人，把捣成的纯橄榄油拿来给你，为点灯用，使灯常常点着。
verses.text_big5_plain: 你要吩咐以色列人，把搗成的純橄欖油拿來給你，為點燈用，使燈常常點著。

footnotes.zh: 用来点灯之捣成的纯橄榄油，表征纯净的圣灵，出于被压榨的橄榄所预表钉十字架的基督(参约十九34)，使基督在神的居所里作灯台照耀。见太二六36注1与出二五31注2二段。
footnotes.zh_big5: 用來點燈之搗成的純橄欖油，表徵純淨的聖靈，出於被壓榨的橄欖所豫表釘十字架的基督，（參約十九34，）使基督在神的居所裏作燈臺照耀。見太二六36註1與出二五31註2二段。
footnotes.en: 24:2 1 pure The pure oil of beaten olives for the light signifies the pure Holy Spirit coming out of the crucified Christ (cf. John 19:34), typified by the beaten olives, for the shining of Christ as the lampstand in God's dwelling place. See note Matt. 26:36 1 and note Exo. 25:31 1 , par. 2.

footnotes.zh: 直译，使灯(的光)常常上升。
footnotes.zh_big5: 直譯，使燈（的光）常常上升。
footnotes.en: 24:2 2 make Lit., cause the light of a lamp to ascend.

refs.text_gb: 你要吩咐以色列人，把捣成的纯橄榄油拿来给你，为点灯用，使灯常常点着。

refs.text_en: And you shall command the children of Israel to bring to you pure oil of beaten olives for the light, to make the lamps burn continually.

refs.text_gb: 在会幕中见证柜前的幔外，亚伦和他的子孙，从晚上到早晨，要在耶和华面前整理这灯。这要作以色列人世世代代永远的定例。
refs.text_big5: 在會幕中見證櫃前的幔外，亞倫和他的子孫，從晚上到早晨，要在耶和華面前整理這燈。這要作以色列人世世代代永遠的定例。
refs.text_en: In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil which is before the Testimony, Aaron and his sons shall maintain it in order from evening to morning before Jehovah; it shall be a perpetual statute to be observed throughout their generations by the children of Israel.

verses.text_gb: 在会幕中见证柜的幔子外，亚伦从晚上到早晨，要在耶和华面前常常[Fn1]整理这灯。这要作你们世世代代永远的定例。
verses.text_big5: 在會幕中見證櫃的幔子外，亞倫從晚上到早晨，要在耶和華面前常常[Fn1]整理這燈。這要作你們世世代代永遠的定例。
verses.text_en: Outside the veil of the Testimony in the Tent of Meeting Aaron shall maintain it in order from evening to morning before Jehovah continually. It shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations.
verses.text_gb_plain: 在会幕中见证柜的幔子外，亚伦从晚上到早晨，要在耶和华面前常常整理这灯。这要作你们世世代代永远的定例。
verses.text_big5_plain: 在會幕中見證櫃的幔子外，亞倫從晚上到早晨，要在耶和華面前常常整理這燈。這要作你們世世代代永遠的定例。

footnotes.zh: 或，料理。4节者同。灯常常点着(2)，表征基督是神圣的光(约一4，八12)，在神的家中不断照耀。大祭司亚伦常常整理这灯(3～4)，表征我们的大祭司基督常常照料祂神圣的光，好不断为神照耀。
footnotes.zh_big5: 或，料理。4節者同。燈常常點著，（2，）表徵基督是神聖的光，（約一4，八12，）在神的家中不斷照耀。大祭司亞倫常常整理這燈，（3～4，）表徵我們的大祭司基督常常照料祂神聖的光，好不斷為神照耀。
footnotes.en: 24:3 1 set Or, tend it. So also in v. 4. The burning of the lamps continually (v. 2) signifies that Christ as the divine light (John 1:4; 8:12) shines continually in the house of God. The tending of the lamps continually (vv. 3-4) by Aaron, the high priest, signifies that Christ as our High Priest continually takes care of His divine light, causing it to shine for God continually.

verses.text_gb: 他要在耶和华面前常常整理纯金[Cra]灯台上的灯。
verses.text_big5: 他要在耶和華面前常常整理純金[Cra]燈臺上的燈。
verses.text_en: He shall maintain the lamps in order on the pure lampstand before Jehovah continually.
verses.text_gb_plain: 他要在耶和华面前常常整理纯金灯台上的灯。
verses.text_big5_plain: 他要在耶和華面前常常整理純金燈臺上的燈。

refs.text_gb: 你要用纯金作一个灯台。灯台的座和干，与杯、花萼、花苞，都要接连一块锤出来。
refs.text_big5: 你要用純金作一個燈臺。燈臺的座和榦，與杯、花萼、花苞，都要接連一塊錘出來。
refs.text_en: And you shall make a lampstand of pure gold. The lampstand with its base and its shaft shall be made of beaten work; its cups, its calyxes, and its blossom buds shall be of one piece with it.

refs.text_gb: 灯台两边要杈出六个枝子，这边三个，那边三个。
refs.text_big5: 燈臺兩邊要杈出六個枝子，這邊三個，那邊三個。
refs.text_en: And there shall be six branches going out of its sides; three branches of the lampstand out of one of its sides, and three branches of the lampstand out of its other side;

refs.text_gb: 这边每枝上有三个杯，形状像杏花，有花萼，有花苞；那边每枝上也有三个杯，形状像杏花，有花萼，有花苞；从灯台杈出来的六个枝子，都是如此。
refs.text_big5: 這邊每枝上有三個杯，形狀像杏花，有花萼，有花苞；那邊每枝上也有三個杯，形狀像杏花，有花萼，有花苞；從燈臺杈出來的六個枝子，都是如此。
refs.text_en: Three cups made like almond blossoms in one branch, a calyx and a blossom bud; and three cups made like almond blossoms in the other branch, a calyx and a blossom bud-so for the six branches going out of the lampstand.

refs.text_gb: 灯台的干上有四个杯，形状像杏花，有花萼，有花苞。
refs.text_big5: 燈臺的榦上有四個杯，形狀像杏花，有花萼，有花苞。
refs.text_en: And there shall be on the lampstand four cups made like almond blossoms, its calyxes and its blossom buds;

refs.text_gb: 灯台每两个枝子以下有花萼，与灯台接连一块；从灯台杈出来的六个枝子，都是如此；
refs.text_big5: 燈臺每兩個枝子以下有花萼，與燈臺接連一塊；從燈臺杈出來的六個枝子，都是如此；
refs.text_en: And a calyx under two branches of one piece with it, and a calyx under two branches of one piece with it, and a calyx under two branches of one piece with it, for the six branches going out of the lampstand.

refs.text_gb: 花萼和枝子要与灯台接连一块，都是一块纯金锤出来的。
refs.text_big5: 花萼和枝子要與燈臺接連一塊，都是一塊純金錘出來的。
refs.text_en: Their calyxes and their branches shall be of one piece with it; all of it one beaten work of pure gold.

refs.text_gb: 要作灯台的七个灯盏；要把灯盏放上，使灯光对照。
refs.text_big5: 要作燈臺的七個燈盞；要把燈盞放上，使燈光對照。
refs.text_en: And you shall make its lamps, seven; and set up its lamps to give light to the area in front of it.

refs.text_gb: 灯台的灯剪和灯花盘，也是要纯金的。
refs.text_big5: 燈臺的燈剪和燈花盤，也是要純金的。
refs.text_en: And its tongs and its firepans shall be of pure gold.

refs.text_gb: 作灯台和这一切的器具，要用纯金一他连得。
refs.text_big5: 作燈臺和這一切的器具，要用純金一他連得。
refs.text_en: It shall be made of a talent of pure gold, with all these utensils.

verses.text_gb: 你要取细面，烤成十二个[Fn1][Cra]饼，每个饼用细面一伊法的十分之二。
verses.text_big5: 你要取細麵，烤成十二個[Fn1][Cra]餅，每個餅用細麵一伊法的十分之二。
verses.text_en: And you shall take fine flour and bake twelve cakes with it; two-tenths of an ephah shall be in each cake.
verses.text_gb_plain: 你要取细面，烤成十二个饼，每个饼用细面一伊法的十分之二。
verses.text_big5_plain: 你要取細麵，烤成十二個餅，每個餅用細麵一伊法的十分之二。

footnotes.zh: 这表征那产生召会(由细面一伊法的十分之二所预表—二三13，17)的复活基督，乃是完满(十二这数字表征完满—太十四20与注)构成食物的元素，给神所有的子民(由十二个饼所指的十二支派作代表)并给神享受。
footnotes.zh_big5: 這表徵那產生召會（由細麵一伊法的十分之二所豫表—二三13，17）的復活基督，乃是完滿（十二這數字表徵完滿—太十四20與註）構成食物的元素，給神所有的子民（由十二個餅所指的十二支派作代表）並給神享受。
footnotes.en: 24:5 1 cakes This signifies that the resurrected Christ, the Christ who produced the church (typified by the two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour — Lev. 23:13, 17), is the element that constitutes the food in full (the number twelve signifies fullness — Matt. 14:20 and note Matt. 14:20 1 ) for all God's people (represented by the twelve tribes, who are referred to in the twelve cakes) and for God to enjoy.

refs.text_gb: 又要在桌子上，在我面前，常摆陈设饼。
refs.text_big5: 又要在桌子上，在我面前，常擺陳設餅。
refs.text_en: And you shall set the bread of the Presence upon the table before Me always.

verses.text_gb: 要把饼摆成两行，每行六个，放在耶和华面前纯金的[Cra]桌子上；
verses.text_big5: 要把餅擺成兩行，每行六個，放在耶和華面前純金的[Cra]桌子上；
verses.text_en: And you shall set them in two rows, six in a row, on the table of pure gold before Jehovah.
verses.text_gb_plain: 要把饼摆成两行，每行六个，放在耶和华面前纯金的桌子上；
verses.text_big5_plain: 要把餅擺成兩行，每行六個，放在耶和華面前純金的桌子上；

refs.text_gb: 你要用皂荚木作一张桌子，长二肘，宽一肘，高一肘半。
refs.text_big5: 你要用皂莢木作一張桌子，長二肘，寬一肘，高一肘半。
refs.text_en: And you shall make a table of acacia wood: two cubits shall be its length, and a cubit its width, and one and a half cubits its height.

refs.text_gb: 要包上纯金，四围镶上金牙边。
refs.text_big5: 要包上純金，四圍鑲上金牙邊。
refs.text_en: And you shall overlay it with pure gold and make a rim of gold around it.

refs.text_gb: 桌子的四围，要作一掌宽的框子，框子的四围镶着金牙边。
refs.text_big5: 桌子的四圍，要作一掌寬的框子，框子的四圍鑲著金牙邊。
refs.text_en: And you shall make a frame of a handbreadth around it; and you shall make a rim of gold for its frame around it.

refs.text_gb: 要作四个金环，安在桌子四个脚的四角上。
refs.text_big5: 要作四個金環，安在桌子四個腳的四角上。
refs.text_en: And you shall make for it four rings of gold and put the rings on the four corners that are on its four feet.

refs.text_big5: 環子要靠近框子，可以穿槓抬桌子。
refs.text_en: The rings shall be close to the frame as holders for the poles to carry the table.

refs.text_gb: 要用皂荚木作两根杠，用金包裹，以便抬桌子。
refs.text_big5: 要用皂莢木作兩根槓，用金包裹，以便抬桌子。
refs.text_en: And you shall make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, and the table shall be carried with them.

refs.text_gb: 要作桌子上的盘子、调羹、并奠酒的壶和杯；这些都要用纯金制作。
refs.text_big5: 要作桌子上的盤子、調羹、並奠酒的壺和杯；這些都要用純金製作。
refs.text_en: And you shall make its plates and its cups and its pitchers and its bowls with which to pour out drink offerings; of pure gold you shall make them.

refs.text_gb: 他们每日早晚向耶和华烧燔祭，和馨香的香，又在纯金的桌子上摆陈设饼；他们也照料金灯台和灯盏，每晚点起；我们谨守耶和华我们神所交付的职守，你们却离弃了祂。
refs.text_big5: 他們每日早晚向耶和華燒燔祭，和馨香的香，又在純金的桌子上擺陳設餅；他們也照料金燈臺和燈盞，每晚點起；我們謹守耶和華我們神所交付的職守，你們卻離棄了祂。
refs.text_en: And they offer in smoke to Jehovah burnt offerings morning by morning and evening by evening as well as fragrant incense, and they set the rows of bread upon the pure table, and they care for the golden lampstand and its lamps that it may burn evening by evening; for we keep the charge of Jehovah our God, but you have forsaken Him.

refs.text_gb: 因为有预备好的帐幕，头一层叫作圣所，里面有灯台、桌子和陈设饼；
refs.text_big5: 因為有豫備好的帳幕，頭一層叫作聖所，裏面有燈臺、桌子和陳設餅；
refs.text_en: For a tabernacle was prepared, the first, in which the lampstand and the table and the loaves were set forth, which is called the Holy Place;

verses.text_gb: 又要把纯[Fn1][Cra]乳香放在每行的饼上，作为记念，作为[Fn2]献给耶和华的火祭。
verses.text_big5: 又要把純[Fn1][Cra]乳香放在每行的餅上，作為記念，作為[Fn2]獻給耶和華的火祭。
verses.text_en: And you shall put pure frankincense on each row, so that it may be a memorial for the bread, an offering by fire to Jehovah.
verses.text_gb_plain: 又要把纯乳香放在每行的饼上，作为记念，作为献给耶和华的火祭。
verses.text_big5_plain: 又要把純乳香放在每行的餅上，作為記念，作為獻給耶和華的火祭。

footnotes.zh: 基督乃是带着祂复活的香气(乳香)作为记念的部分，成了神和我们的食物。
footnotes.zh_big5: 基督乃是帶著祂復活的香氣（乳香）作為記念的部分，成了神和我們的食物。
footnotes.en: 24:7 1 frankincense It is with the fragrance of His resurrection (frankincense) as a memorial portion that Christ becomes food to both God and us.

footnotes.zh: 陈设饼是给神和祭司(9)的食物，指明神的祭司在事奉神的事上与神是一；他们所吃的就是神所吃的，他们所享受的也是神所享受的。
footnotes.zh_big5: 陳設餅是給神和祭司（9）的食物，指明神的祭司在事奉神的事上與神是一；他們所喫的就是神所喫的，他們所享受的也是神所享受的。
footnotes.en: 24:7 2 offering That the bread of the Presence was food for both God and the priests (v. 9) indicates that God's priests are one with Him in His service; what they eat is what God eats, and what they enjoy is what God enjoys.

refs.text_gb: 带到亚伦子孙作祭司的那里；祭司就要从细面中取出一把来，并取些油和所有的乳香，然后把所取的这些作为素祭记念的部分，烧在坛上，是献与耶和华为怡爽香气的火祭。
refs.text_big5: 帶到亞倫子孫作祭司的那裏；祭司就要從細麵中取出一把來，並取些油和所有的乳香，然後把所取的這些作為素祭記念的部分，燒在壇上，是獻與耶和華為怡爽香氣的火祭。
refs.text_en: Then he shall bring it to Aaron's sons the priests, and he shall take from it his handful of its fine flour and of its oil with all its frankincense. And the priest shall burn it as its memorial portion on the altar, an offering by fire, a satisfying fragrance to Jehovah.

verses.text_gb: 每[Fn1]安息日要常常把饼摆列在耶和华面前；这要为以色列人作永远的约。
verses.text_big5: 每[Fn1]安息日要常常把餅擺列在耶和華面前；這要為以色列人作永遠的約。
verses.text_en: Every Sabbath day continually he shall set it in order before Jehovah; it is an everlasting covenant for the children of Israel.
verses.text_gb_plain: 每安息日要常常把饼摆列在耶和华面前；这要为以色列人作永远的约。
verses.text_big5_plain: 每安息日要常常把餅擺列在耶和華面前；這要為以色列人作永遠的約。

footnotes.zh: 安息日这辞带进安息的思想。这表征我们享受基督作我们的食物，应当重新整理，使我们能常常与神有安息。
footnotes.zh_big5: 安息日這辭帶進安息的思想。這表徵我們享受基督作我們的食物，應當重新整理，使我們能常常與神有安息。
footnotes.en: 24:8 1 Sabbath The word Sabbath brings in the thought of rest. This signifies that our enjoyment of Christ as our food should be set in order afresh that we may have rest with God continually.

verses.text_gb: 这饼是要给亚伦和他子孙的，他们要[Cra]在[Fn1]圣处吃，因为这在献给耶和华的火祭中是至圣的，要归与亚伦；这是永远的定例。
verses.text_big5: 這餅是要給亞倫和他子孫的，他們要[Cra]在[Fn1]聖處喫，因為這在獻給耶和華的火祭中是至聖的，要歸與亞倫；這是永遠的定例。
verses.text_en: And it shall be for Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place, for it is most holy to him of Jehovah's offerings by fire, a perpetual statute.
verses.text_gb_plain: 这饼是要给亚伦和他子孙的，他们要在圣处吃，因为这在献给耶和华的火祭中是至圣的，要归与亚伦；这是永远的定例。
verses.text_big5_plain: 這餅是要給亞倫和他子孫的，他們要在聖處喫，因為這在獻給耶和華的火祭中是至聖的，要歸與亞倫；這是永遠的定例。

footnotes.zh: 这表征我们事奉神的人，应当在召会这圣处，享受基督作献给神的食物中至圣的部分。
footnotes.zh_big5: 這表徵我們事奉神的人，應當在召會這聖處，享受基督作獻給神的食物中至聖的部分。
footnotes.en: 24:9 1 holy This signifies that we, God's serving ones, should enjoy Christ as a most holy portion of the food offered to God, in the church as the holy place.

refs.text_gb: 祭司就拿圣饼给他；因为在那里没有别的饼，只有陈设饼，是当时为了放上热的饼，从耶和华面前撤下来的。
refs.text_big5: 祭司就拿聖餅給他；因為在那裏沒有別的餅，只有陳設餅，是當時為了放上熱的餅，從耶和華面前撤下來的。
refs.text_en: So the priest gave him what was holy, for there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence, which was taken from before Jehovah, to be replaced by hot bread at the time it was taken.

refs.text_gb: 他怎样进了神的殿，他们且吃了陈设饼，就是他不可吃，跟从他的人也不可吃，唯独祭司才可吃的。
refs.text_big5: 他怎樣進了神的殿，他們且喫了陳設餅，就是他不可喫，跟從他的人也不可喫，惟獨祭司纔可喫的。
refs.text_en: How he entered into the house of God, and they ate the bread of the Presence, which was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those who were with him, except for the priests only?

refs.text_gb: 他当大祭司亚比亚他的时候，怎样进了神的殿，且吃了祭司以外人不可吃的陈设饼，又给跟从他的人吃。
refs.text_big5: 他當大祭司亞比亞他的時候，怎樣進了神的殿，且喫了祭司以外人不可喫的陳設餅，又給跟從他的人喫。
refs.text_en: How he entered into the house of God during the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the bread of the Presence, which is not lawful for anyone to eat except the priests, and he gave also to those who were with him?

refs.text_gb: 他怎样进了神的殿，且拿祭司以外，别人都不可吃的陈设饼吃，又给跟从他的人吃。
refs.text_big5: 他怎樣進了神的殿，且拿祭司以外，別人都不可喫的陳設餅喫，又給跟從他的人喫。
refs.text_en: How he entered into the house of God, and taking the bread of the Presence, he ate it and gave some to those with him, which is not lawful for anyone to eat except the priests alone?

verses.text_gb: [Fn1]有一个以色列妇人的儿子，他父亲是埃及人，一日出到以色列人中间；这以色列妇人的儿子和一个以色列人在营里争斗。
verses.text_big5: [Fn1]有一個以色列婦人的兒子，他父親是埃及人，一日出到以色列人中間；這以色列婦人的兒子和一個以色列人在營裏爭鬥。
verses.text_en: Now the son of an Israelite woman, who was also the son of an Egyptian man, went out among the children of Israel; and the son of the Israelite woman and a certain Israelite struggled together in the camp.
verses.text_gb_plain: 有一个以色列妇人的儿子，他父亲是埃及人，一日出到以色列人中间；这以色列妇人的儿子和一个以色列人在营里争斗。
verses.text_big5_plain: 有一個以色列婦人的兒子，他父親是埃及人，一日出到以色列人中間；這以色列婦人的兒子和一個以色列人在營裏爭鬥。

footnotes.zh: 这个事件表征，属神的人与属世的人结合所产生的结果会使神受到玷辱，使玷辱神的人从对基督完满的享受里隔断(16)，不能享受祂作照耀的光和滋养的食物。
footnotes.zh_big5: 這個事件表徵，屬神的人與屬世的人結合所產生的結果會使神受到玷辱，使玷辱神的人從對基督完滿的享受裏隔斷，（16，）不能享受祂作照耀的光和滋養的食物。
footnotes.en: 24:10 1 Now This story signifies that the joining of a man of God with a man of the world brings forth a result that will profane God, causing the profaning one to be cut off (v. 16) from the enjoyment of Christ in His fullness as the shining light and nourishing food.

verses.text_gb: 这以色列妇人的儿子[Fn1][Cra]亵渎了圣名，并且咒诅，就有人把他送到摩西那里。（他母亲名叫示罗密，是但支派底伯利的女儿。）
verses.text_big5: 這以色列婦人的兒子[Fn1][Cra]褻瀆了聖名，並且咒詛，就有人把他送到摩西那裏。（他母親名叫示羅密，是但支派底伯利的女兒。）
verses.text_en: And the son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name and cursed, and they brought him to Moses. (Now his mother's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.)
verses.text_gb_plain: 这以色列妇人的儿子亵渎了圣名，并且咒诅，就有人把他送到摩西那里。（他母亲名叫示罗密，是但支派底伯利的女儿。）
verses.text_big5_plain: 這以色列婦人的兒子褻瀆了聖名，並且咒詛，就有人把他送到摩西那裏。（他母親名叫示羅密，是但支派底伯利的女兒。）

footnotes.zh: 亵渎圣名的事件记载于安排陈设饼的记载之后，表征为了完满的享受基督作我们的光和食物(1～9)，我们需要尊主的名为圣而不亵渎这名(参太六9)。尊主的名为圣，就是尊重并尊敬圣名，把这名当作独一的名分别出来，不与其他凡俗的名同列。
footnotes.zh_big5: 褻瀆聖名的事件記載於安排陳設餅的記載之後，表徵為了完滿的享受基督作我們的光和食物，（1～9，）我們需要尊主的名為聖而不褻瀆這名。（參太六9。）尊主的名為聖，就是尊重並尊敬聖名，把這名當作獨一的名分別出來，不與其他凡俗的名同列。
footnotes.en: 24:11 1 blasphemed That the story of the blaspheming of the holy Name is recorded after the record concerning the arranging of the bread of the Presence signifies that in order to enjoy Christ in His fullness as our light and as our food (vv. 1-9), we need to sanctify the holy Name and not profane it (cf. Matt. 6:9). To sanctify the Lord's name is to honor and respect the holy Name by separating it as something unique, not putting it with other, common names.

refs.text_gb: 耶和华说，我的百姓既是无价被掳去，如今我在这里作什么呢？耶和华说，辖制他们的人咆哮，我的名终日不住地受亵渎。
refs.text_big5: 耶和華說，我的百姓既是無價被擄去，如今我在這裏作甚麼呢？耶和華說，轄制他們的人咆哮，我的名終日不住的受褻瀆。
refs.text_en: Now then what do I have here, declares Jehovah, since My people have been taken away for nothing? Those who rule over them howl, declares Jehovah, and My name is continually blasphemed all day long.

refs.text_gb: 如经上所记：“神的名在外邦人中，因你们受了亵渎。”
refs.text_big5: 如經上所記：“神的名在外邦人中，因你們受了褻瀆。”
refs.text_en: For "the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you," even as it is written.

refs.text_gb: 他们不是亵渎那在你们身上被称呼的尊名么？
refs.text_big5: 他們不是褻瀆那在你們身上被稱呼的尊名麼？
refs.text_en: Is it not they who blaspheme the honorable name by which you are called?

refs.text_gb: 人被大热所烤，就亵渎那有权掌管这些灾之神的名，并不悔改将荣耀归与神。
refs.text_big5: 人被大熱所烤，就褻瀆那有權掌管這些災之神的名，並不悔改將榮耀歸與神。
refs.text_en: And men were burned with great heat, and they blasphemed the name of God, who has the authority over these plagues, and they did not repent so as to give Him glory.

refs.text_gb: 不可妄称耶和华你神的名；因为妄称耶和华名的，耶和华必不以他为无罪。
refs.text_big5: 不可妄稱耶和華你神的名；因為妄稱耶和華名的，耶和華必不以他為無罪。
refs.text_en: You shall not take the name of Jehovah your God in vain, for Jehovah will not hold guiltless him who takes His name in vain.

refs.text_gb: 不可辱骂神，也不可毁谤你百姓的官长。
refs.text_big5: 不可辱罵神，也不可毀謗你百姓的官長。
refs.text_en: You shall not revile God, nor curse a ruler of your people.

verses.text_big5: 他們把那人拘禁起來，要得耶和華所指示的話。
